title: Indicators framework & v1 indicator set
body:
## Context
R1 "Charting alpha" makes a trader able to *read* the market. E13 is the indicators slice of that: the runtime that turns a declarative indicator spec into incrementally-computed series, the UI to add/configure/remove them, and the v1 indicator set. Roadmap scope line (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2): "Indicator runtime (declarative spec -> incremental computation, backend M9 for heavy series, frontend for cheap ones); overlay vs separate-pane placement; parameter editing with live re-compute; v1 set: MA/EMA/WMA/VWAP (+session/anchored), Bollinger, ATR, RSI, MACD, Stochastic, volume + volume MA, OBV; indicator templates; per-indicator styling from design tokens". Train window S07-S08, 47 points, area `area/charting-ui`, backend module **M9** `orderflow` (CONSTITUTION.md §3), story domain **IND**.

Two hard constraints shape the whole epic:
1. **One kernel, one result.** US-IND-002's NFR: "shared indicator kernel used by chart, alerts, rule engine and backtest - one implementation, one result." `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 makes the `MetricRegistry` the single named registry behind the rule vocabulary, the alert editor, the journal and the indicator list. E13 therefore does not build a chart-only TA library; it builds the metric kernel plus a worker-side mirror.
2. **Rule-feeding indicators are authoritative in the backend.** `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` open question O4: the rule engine runs server-side and must never depend on a browser, so any indicator referenced by a rule IR is computed authoritatively in the backend and the worker copy is a display-only mirror that must reproduce it bit-for-bit under the parity test (§14). E13 resolves O4 and records the resolution as an ADR.

Depends on E12 (bar builders and series rendering) per `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 `E12 --> E13`, and gates E15 (`E13 --> E15`, layouts persist the indicator stack and sub-pane heights). The order-flow indicators (footprint, profiles, CVD pane, OI/funding/liquidation series) are NOT in E13 - they arrive with E18/E19/E23/E24 in R2 and plug into the API this epic defines.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Goal** - a trader can add any v1 indicator to a chart, tune it live, style it from tokens, save it as a preset, read it from the legend or a screen reader, and reference its value by name from the alert/rule editors, with values identical to the backend's.

- **Runtime**: `IndicatorPlugin` API and worker-hosted runtime in `packages/chart-engine` (`src/plugins/`), incremental `update(lastBar)` with `recompute(range)` fallback, `BarSeries.densify()` handling for gapped series, pane placement (overlay / sub-pane), output buffers rendered via CMP-194 IndicatorOverlay.
- **Backend kernel**: `services/api/orderflow/` (M9) indicator kernel + `MetricDescriptor`/`MetricRegistry` registration for `sma`, `ema`, `wma`, `vwma`, `smma`, `dema`, `tema`, `vwap`, `bollinger`, `keltner`, `donchian`, `atr`, `adx`, `rsi`, `macd`, `stochastic`, `cci`, `williams_r`, `supertrend`, `zigzag`, `ichimoku`, `psar`, `volume`, `volume_ma`, `obv`, `cmf`, `mfi`, `cvd`.
- **Catalogue endpoint**: `GET /api/v1/indicators` (`listIndicators`, `IndicatorDescriptor`) so settings forms render from JSON Schema and adding an indicator needs no frontend release.
- **Presets**: `indicator_presets` table (§3.8.4), `/indicator-presets` CRUD, built-in presets of §10.5, `is_favourite`, `pane_target`.
- **Screens**: SCR-034 indicator library, SCR-035 indicator settings dialog, SCR-036 indicator manager (object tree - also the a11y-complete alternative to canvas manipulation).
- **Components consumed**: CMP-194, CMP-197, CMP-199, CMP-224 plus the atoms/molecules listed per screen in `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`.
- **Stories realised**: US-IND-001 (Must), US-IND-002, US-IND-003, US-IND-004, US-IND-005, US-IND-006, US-IND-007 (Must/Should) and US-IND-008 (Must).

## Out of scope
- Order-flow indicators and panes: footprint (E18), volume/delta/TPO profiles (E19), CVD dedicated pane (E23), OI/funding/liquidations (E24), detectors/regime (E25). E13 only ships the `cvd`/`volume` *classic indicator* forms whose values must later match those panes exactly.
- User-authored indicator scripting - explicitly a non-goal (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §1: "No indicator scripting language (indicators are TypeScript plugins)"); scripting is the P4 scripting epic.
- Alert and rule *editors* themselves (E40 / E35-E37). E13 only guarantees the metric vocabulary and the metric-in-use referential guard.
- Chart templates and workspace persistence of the indicator stack - E15.
- Backtesting use of the kernel - P4.
- Android; any separate admin app; non-Bybit / non-USDT-perp instruments.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The v1 set is complete and correct
  Given the recorded Bybit BTCUSDT fixture symbol-day used by the R1 integration suite
  When every v1 indicator is computed by the backend kernel and by the worker mirror
  Then both agree with the reference implementation to 1e-8 and with each other bit-for-bit

Scenario: A trader tunes an indicator live
  Given EMA(21) is on a 100k-bar chart
  When the period is changed to 34 in SCR-035
  Then the visible window recomputes in <=100 ms, off-screen ranges backfill in the worker, and no chart reload occurs

Scenario: Ten indicators do not break the frame budget
  Given ten indicators are active across the price pane and two sub-panes
  Then the engine benchmark reports >=55 fps and p95 frame time <=16.6 ms on reference hardware in Electron

Scenario: Indicators are operable without a mouse
  Given a keyboard-only user on SCR-036
  Then every indicator can be added, reordered, hidden, configured and removed, and the legend value is announced by the screen reader

Scenario: A metric in use cannot vanish
  Given an armed rule references ema(21, 5m)
  When the trader removes that indicator
  Then removal is blocked with the list of referencing rules and links to disarm or edit them
```

## Technical notes / design
Pipeline: `BarStore` (E12) -> worker `IndicatorHost` -> `OutputBuffers` -> `IndicatorOverlay`/sub-pane render pass. Backend: bars from M8 -> `IndicatorKernel` (M9) -> `MetricRegistry` binding -> memoised per `(symbol, spec_hash, params)` so ten rules on `atr(14)` cost one computation (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7). Determinism rules: no indicator may read wall-clock time; warmup is declared as `warmup_bars` and values before it are `None`, never 0; provisional values (ZigZag's unconfirmed leg) carry `provisional=true` and are excluded from rule evaluation.

## Test plan
Golden-vector unit tests per indicator (fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/`), property-based tests for incremental-vs-full equivalence, cross-language parity tests (Python kernel vs TypeScript mirror), contract tests for `GET /indicators` and `/indicator-presets`, Playwright E2E for add/configure/remove/preset flows in web and Electron, engine FPS benchmark with 10 indicators, axe-core on SCR-034/035/036.

## Security notes
Low-sensitivity data class (market data + user presentation preferences), but three real surfaces: (a) `params_schema` is server-supplied JSON Schema rendered into a form - must not be a rendering-time injection vector; (b) `indicator_presets.params`/`style` are user-controlled JSONB - size- and shape-bounded, RBAC-scoped to the owning user (`workspaces:read`/`write`, scope self); (c) unbounded indicator parameters (period 5000 x many instances) are a client and server CPU-exhaustion vector. STRIDE model in E13-X01.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-036 is the designated accessible equivalent for canvas objects (`role="tree"`, every object reachable and editable by keyboard). Indicator series must be distinguishable without colour - dash patterns vary alongside the token colour (SCR-035). Divergence and Supertrend flips use a glyph plus text label, never colour alone (US-IND-003, US-IND-005). Legend values are exposed in the DOM-mirror a11y layer built by E11.

## Performance notes
Budget #1 (p95 <=16.6 ms frame) and #2 (30 fps floor) are hard gates; §4.3 allocates <=2 ms per frame to profile/CVD/indicator pane redraw. SCR-034: first visible window computed in <=250 ms on a 100k-bar series; SCR-035: parameter edit recomputes the visible window in <=100 ms. US-IND-001 NFR: ten indicators must not drop below 55 fps.

## Observability
Metrics `indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,where}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}`, `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`. Analytics events `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.reordered`, `indicator.visibility_toggled`, `indicator.removed` per SCR-034/035/036. A parity mismatch is logged at ERROR with both values and the bar index.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level AC verified end-to-end on the recorded fixture day, demoed to the Owner.
- [ ] Coverage floors held (>=85% engine/backend, >=80% frontend); zero open P0/P1 bugs in E13 scope.
- [ ] O4 resolved and recorded as an ADR; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core zero violations on SCR-034/035/036 plus a manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass.
- [ ] perf: 10-indicator benchmark wired into the CI engine benchmark as a required check.
- [ ] STRIDE model finalised and findings triaged; Security engineer sign-off.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression and exploratory pass executed and recorded.

## Dependencies
- **E12** bar builders and series rendering - supplies `BarStore`/`BarSeries.densify()` and the series render passes (`E12 --> E13`).
- **E11** chart engine core - plugin host, pane stacking, legend, DOM-mirror a11y layer.
- **E05** design system v0 - tokens, `color.indicator.palette[]`, dialog/drawer primitives.
- Gates **E15** layouts (indicator stack + sub-pane heights persist per layout) and, in R2, E18/E19/E23/E24 which register their series through this plugin API.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). The first consuming frontend stories (E13-S01, E13-S02) start in **Sprint 07**, which is **2 full sprints** after design Done, so the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule is satisfied on its own terms and **no Architect/CDO waiver is required** for E13-S01, E13-S02, E13-S03, E13-S04, E13-S06, E13-S07 or E13-S08. Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.
## Branch
`feat/e13-indicators-*` per child ticket; PRs <=400 LOC diff.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: UX research: how traders add, tune and manage indicators
body:
## Context
E13 introduces three net-new surfaces (SCR-034 library, SCR-035 settings, SCR-036 object tree) and a new interaction class: live parameter tuning of a computed series over a 100k-bar chart. Before wireframes are drawn we need evidence on how the Owner and the account managers actually work with indicators today in TradingView/DeepCharts - what they add first, how often they re-tune, whether they use templates, and how they find an indicator among ~28. `docs/plan/10-personas.md` gives the personas; this ticket produces the behavioural facts the wireframes are argued from.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3-4 moderated sessions (Owner + up to 2 account managers + 1 proxy trader), 45 min each, screen-shared against their current tooling.
- Task-based probes: add EMA(21); change its period; find ATR among a full catalogue; remove an indicator that an alert depends on; reproduce a saved setup on a second symbol.
- Competitive teardown of indicator library + settings dialogs (TradingView, DeepCharts/Sierra, ATAS) covering search, categorisation, favourites, preview, and "second instance" handling.
- Findings written to `docs/design/research/e13-indicators.md`: ranked task frequencies, the "top 8 indicators actually used" list, naming/labelling vocabulary, and 5-8 adopted design decisions each phrased as a testable statement.
- A decision on whether indicator *templates* (a saved stack) are needed at v1 or whether `indicator_presets` (per-indicator, §3.8.4) plus E15 chart templates already cover it - this directly decides whether E13 grows a stack-level surface.

## Out of scope
- Drawing tools (E14), layouts/workspaces (E15), alert editor (E40) research.
- Visual design of any kind - greyscale wireframes start in E13-D02.
- Recruiting external participants outside the owner's circle.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Evidence exists for every wireframe decision
  When docs/design/research/e13-indicators.md is reviewed
  Then it lists at least 5 adopted decisions, each traceable to a specific observation, and each phrased so a wireframe can satisfy or violate it

Scenario: The catalogue-findability question is answered
  Given participants were asked to find ATR in a ~28-entry catalogue
  Then the report states whether search, category grouping or favourites was the winning path and recommends the default landing state of SCR-034

Scenario: The templates question is resolved
  Then the report recommends either "indicator templates in E13" or "covered by indicator_presets + E15 chart templates", with the reasoning recorded, and the recommendation is carried into E13-D02's scope

Scenario: A finding contradicts the plan
  Given a finding contradicts docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-034/035/036 as written
  Then the contradiction is raised as a catalogue amendment proposal rather than silently designed around
```

## Technical notes / design
Sessions recorded per `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md`; recordings stored in the design drive, not the repo; only anonymised quotes land in the report. Use a fixed script so the five task probes are comparable across participants.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validity control: two researchers independently tag the session notes and reconcile; any decision supported by a single observation is marked "weak evidence" and re-tested in E13-D06 design QA.

## Security notes
Recordings may show real account balances and symbol lists - blur or exclude any account/balance region before storing, per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` data-classification rules. No credentials are to be entered during a session.

## Accessibility notes
At least one probe is run keyboard-only to seed the SCR-036 object-tree requirements; the a11y specialist reviews the findings for anything that would make the canvas-free path second-class.

## Performance notes
Capture participants' tolerance for re-compute latency ("does a 250 ms library-add feel instant?") to validate the SCR-034/035 budgets rather than assuming them.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every frame/state listed in Scope exists and is reviewed against the per-screen "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- [ ] CDO (or delegate) sign-off recorded on the ticket; artefact linked from the SCR entry.
- [ ] Component usage mapped to real CMP-* ids; any gap filed against E05 rather than drawn ad hoc.
- [ ] a11y reviewer has signed the contrast / focus / non-colour-encoding checks.
- [ ] Handoff notes (tokens, spacing, states, motion, empty/error copy) attached; engineering has acknowledged.
- [ ] Status Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule).

## Dependencies
E05-D01 (Figma Foundations, Sprint 01) gives the greyscale kit used for stimulus material - this is the only E05 artefact needed, which is why this ticket can run in Sprint 02 rather than waiting for the whole E05 epic. No engineering dependency.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). The first consuming frontend stories (E13-S01, E13-S02) start in **Sprint 07**, which is **2 full sprints** after design Done, so the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule is satisfied on its own terms and **no Architect/CDO waiver is required** for E13-S01, E13-S02, E13-S03, E13-S04, E13-S06, E13-S07 or E13-S08. Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.

body:
## Context
Low-fidelity structure for the three E13 surfaces, resolved before pixels are spent. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` already fixes the anatomy of SCR-034 (searchable modal grouped Overlay / Sub-pane / Order-flow), SCR-035 (Inputs / Style / Visibility / Scale / Alerts tabs) and SCR-036 (drawer, `role="tree"`, the accessible equivalent for canvas objects). Figma file `CandleViewer - E13 Indicators (Wires)`, greyscale, auto-layout, at 1280x800 and 2560x1440:

- **SCR-035 Indicator settings**: the four tabs plus Alerts entry point to SCR-091; live preview region; inline validation ("Period must be between 1 and 5000."); "save as default for this indicator" control; reset; the multi-output case (MACD: line + signal + histogram) and the multi-series case (MA ribbon of 5 lengths as one expandable legend entry).
- **SCR-036 Indicator manager**: tree with Overlays / Sub-panes / Drawings / Alerts groups, per-item eye/lock/rename/reorder/delete, multi-select and bulk actions, empty state, and the blocked-removal state when an armed rule references the indicator (US-IND-008).
- Legend/chip surfaces that these screens drive: CMP-224 IndicatorChips row and CMP-199 ChartLegend entries including the errored-indicator and insufficient-history states ("34 more bars needed").
- Component-usage map naming the CMP-* id behind every element, so E05 gaps surface in S05 not S07.

## Out of scope
- Colour, type, iconography, elevation - E13-D03. Motion - E13-D04.
- Order-flow indicator entries beyond showing that the category exists (their content is E18/E19/E23/E24).

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Insufficient history is a designed state, not an error
  Given an indicator whose period exceeds the loaded history (US-IND-002)
  Then a frame shows the series starting at the first valid bar with a legend statement of how many more bars are needed

Scenario: Blocked removal is drawn
  Given an indicator referenced by an armed rule
  Then the SCR-036 frame shows removal blocked with the referencing rules listed and per-rule disarm/edit affordances reachable from the dialog

Scenario: A needed component does not exist
  Given a frame needs a component with no CMP-* entry
  Then the component-usage map records it as a gap with a proposed id and a follow-up ticket is filed against E05
```

## Technical notes / design
Frames use E05 spacing/size variables only, so D03 is purely a theming pass. Each frame carries an annotation layer naming CMP ids, the story id (US-IND-nnn) and the data source (`GET /api/v1/indicators`, `/api/v1/indicator-presets`).

## Test plan
Design review walkthrough against the per-screen sign-off checklists in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`; a second designer runs a states-completeness cross-check; engineering lead confirms each frame is estimable.

The settings form renders from server-supplied `params_schema` - the wireframe must show a bounded, typed control set (numeric stepper, select, colour token) and no free-form HTML/markdown field, so the implementation has no reason to render untrusted strings as markup.

## Accessibility notes
Tab order annotated on every frame; SCR-036 annotated as `role="tree"` with the full keyboard contract (arrow navigation, Enter to open settings, Space to toggle visibility, Delete to remove); every icon-only control has its accessible name written on the frame.

## Performance notes
Wireframes must not assume a synchronous compute: SCR-034's add action and SCR-035's parameter edit each need a designed in-flight state consistent with the <=250 ms / <=100 ms budgets.

## Observability
Annotate which interaction emits `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.reordered`, `indicator.visibility_toggled`, `indicator.removed`.

title: Hi-fi design for SCR-034/035/036 and the indicator visual language
body:
## Context
Hi-fidelity, token-true design of the three indicator surfaces plus the on-chart visual language for indicator series. The roadmap requires "per-indicator styling from design tokens" - this ticket defines that vocabulary once so that every v1 indicator, and every R2 order-flow series that later registers through the same plugin API, inherits it rather than inventing colours.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for SCR-034, SCR-035, SCR-036 in light and dark themes at both densities defined in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- **Indicator palette spec**: the ordered `color.indicator.palette[]` token ramp (CMP-194 consumes it), with assignment rules (nth-indicator gets nth token; a second instance of the same indicator gets the next slot, not the same colour), contrast verified against both chart backgrounds, and a greyscale-safe dash-pattern ladder so two series are distinguishable with colour removed.
- **Series style spec** per output type: line, stepped line, area, band/channel fill (Bollinger/Keltner/Donchian with a shaded channel that keeps candle contrast, per US-IND-004), histogram (volume, MACD), markers (Supertrend flip, ZigZag pivots), dashed "provisional" treatment for an unconfirmed ZigZag leg with its "provisional" label.
- **Legend and chip spec**: CMP-199 legend row and CMP-224 chip anatomy - swatch, name, parameters, current value, visibility toggle, settings, remove; the ribbon case (one entry, expandable list); the errored case (error stated in text); the warming-up case.
- Sub-pane spec: guide levels at 30/70 for RSI, zero line for MACD, the divergence glyph + text label, pane header, and the collapse behaviour when the last indicator in a sub-pane is removed.
- Empty/loading/error/edge-density variants for all three screens.

## Out of scope
- Motion - E13-D04. Order-flow series styling (footprint cells, heatmap) - R2 epics.
- Any new atom not already in `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` unless raised as an E05 contribution.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Colour is never the only carrier
  When the hi-fi chart frames are rendered in greyscale
  Then every simultaneously-visible series remains distinguishable by dash pattern or glyph, and every state (provisional, errored, warming up) is stated in text

Scenario: Contrast passes in both themes
  When every text and non-text UI element on SCR-034/035/036 is measured
  Then contrast meets WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text) in light and dark, evidenced by a measured table in the file

Scenario: Ten indicators still read
  Given a frame with ten active indicators across the price pane and two sub-panes
  Then the legend and chip row have a specified overflow behaviour and no series colour repeats within a pane

Scenario: Every token is real
  Then every colour, spacing and type value references an E05 token name, and any new token is filed as an E05 design-system contribution ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
The palette must be defined as an ordered list with a deterministic assignment function, because the engine assigns colours at add-time without a designer in the loop; the spec states the function, not just the swatches. Band fills specify an alpha that keeps candle body/wick contrast at the worst case (dense candles behind a Bollinger channel).

## Test plan
Contrast measured with a token-level automated check; greyscale export reviewed by the a11y specialist (E13-D05); a designer renders the 10-indicator stress frame and confirms legibility.

## Security notes
N/A - visual design introduces no new trust boundary. Note only that colour tokens must not be user-supplied free strings when preset styles are persisted in `indicator_presets.style`; the spec enumerates allowed token names.

## Accessibility notes
Focus states drawn for every interactive element; the dash-pattern ladder is the primary non-colour carrier; divergence and Supertrend flips get a glyph plus a text label per US-IND-003/005; reduced-motion variants noted for D04.

## Performance notes
Band fills and dashes must be expressible by the engine's instanced thick-line and fill passes (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.x draw-call table) - no design that would force a per-series extra draw call beyond the budgeted <=40 for the combined B5 scene.

## Observability
N/A.

title: Design-system contribution: indicator palette tokens and motion spec
body:
## Context
E13's visual decisions must land in the design system, not in the epic's own CSS, because R2's order-flow series (E18/E19/E23/E24) register through the same plugin API and must inherit the same palette and motion rules. This ticket promotes the E13-D03 output into E05 artefacts and specifies the motion of the three surfaces.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `color.indicator.palette[]` published as an E05 token set (light + dark), with the assignment function documented alongside it and a Storybook swatch page.
- Dash-pattern and marker ladders published as tokens/variants consumed by CMP-194 IndicatorOverlay and CMP-195 AnnotationMarker.
- CMP-199 ChartLegend and CMP-224 IndicatorChips variant additions (ribbon/expandable, errored, warming-up, provisional) added to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` and their Storybook stories specified.
- **Motion spec**: SCR-034/035/036 open/close transitions; the sub-pane create/collapse height animation when the first/last indicator in a pane is added/removed; the series re-compute transition on a parameter change (whether the series morphs or hard-cuts - specified, not left to the implementer); the chip add/remove transition. Each with duration, easing token and a `prefers-reduced-motion` variant that is a non-animated state change, never a removed affordance.
- Copy deck: every string on the three screens including the validation messages ("Period must be between 1 and 5000."), the insufficient-history message, the provisional label, and the blocked-removal message.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the tokens in code (that is the consuming engineering stories and E05's pipeline).
- Motion for drawings (E14) or layouts (E15).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Tokens are in the system, not the epic
  Then color.indicator.palette[] and the dash/marker ladders exist as E05 tokens with light and dark values and a Storybook page, and no E13 frame references a raw hex value

Scenario: Every motion has a reduced-motion counterpart
  When prefers-reduced-motion is simulated for each specified transition
  Then the spec defines an instant state change that preserves the same information, with no loss of an affordance

Scenario: Sub-pane collapse is specified
  Given the last indicator in a sub-pane is removed (US-IND-003)
  Then the spec states the collapse duration, easing, and how the reclaimed vertical space is redistributed across remaining panes

Scenario: Copy is complete
  Then every string in the three screens is in the copy deck; any string discovered missing during implementation is a defect against this ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
Durations must respect the frame budget: no transition may drive a per-frame recompute of indicator series; the series re-compute transition is specified as a buffer swap with a cross-fade of the existing draw, not a re-interpolation of computed values (which would misrepresent data).

## Test plan
Storybook visual review of the swatch/variant pages; a11y specialist reviews reduced-motion variants; the copy deck is proof-read by the product owner.

## Security notes
Enumerated token names only in `indicator_presets.style` - this spec provides the closed list the API validates against, which is what makes the persisted style safe.

## Accessibility notes
Reduced-motion variants mandatory; animation must never be the only signal that a value changed; the palette ramp is validated for both deuteranopia and protanopia simulation in addition to greyscale.

## Performance notes
Transitions are GPU-composited (opacity/transform) only; no layout-thrashing animations near the chart canvas.

N/A.

R1 exit criterion 9 requires every chart to be operable without a mouse. This review signs that claim off at design time, before engineering builds against it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Keyboard contract table for SCR-034 (listbox semantics, each entry announcing its pane target), SCR-035 (tab panel, form field labelling, colour pickers exposing token names) and SCR-036 (`role="tree"`, arrow navigation, expand/collapse, multi-select, bulk actions).
- Screen-reader script per surface: what NVDA and VoiceOver should announce on focus, on value change, and on the live-region events (indicator added, removed, errored, warming up).
- Confirmation that every mouse-only interaction on the chart canvas that E13 introduces (drag a sub-pane divider, click a legend to toggle visibility, click a chip's settings) has an equal-status keyboard path, with the path named.
- Contrast and non-colour-encoding audit of the E13-D03 frames, including the greyscale and colour-vision-deficiency simulations.
- Findings log with severity, each either fixed in the design or filed with an owner.

## Out of scope

```gherkin
Scenario: No canvas-only capability
  When every E13 interaction is enumerated
  Then each has a documented keyboard path of equal status, and SCR-036 covers every indicator object operation (add, configure, reorder, hide, lock, rename, remove)

Scenario: State is never colour-only
  When the frames are reviewed in greyscale and under deuteranopia/protanopia simulation
  Then provisional, errored, warming-up, hidden and locked states each remain identifiable by glyph or text

Scenario: Announcements are specified, not improvised

Scenario: A blocking finding stops sign-off
```

Design-time walkthrough with the a11y specialist using the keyboard contract table as the script; simulated screen-reader read-through of the announcement strings.

N/A.

This ticket *is* the accessibility artefact; its output is the acceptance script reused verbatim by E13-Q04.

## Context
The design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1) forbids frontend work on a screen until its design ticket is Done, >=2 sprints ahead. E13 engineering starts in Sprint 07, so the handoff pack must be complete and signed off by the end of **Sprint 05** - two full sprints ahead, not one. This ticket is the gate, and its sprint placement is what makes the design-ahead rule true rather than merely asserted.

- Redlined specs for SCR-034, SCR-035, SCR-036: spacing, type, token names, component ids, breakpoints, and state matrix.

- Asset export: icons and preview thumbnails referenced by SCR-034 entries.
- The copy deck (from D04) and the accessibility acceptance script (from D05) attached as the QA-usable checklist.
- An engineering walkthrough session with the FE lead and the chart-engine lead; open questions answered in writing on the ticket.
- The per-screen "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` ticked for all three screens.

```gherkin
Scenario: Engineering can build without asking
  Given the FE lead walks through the pack

Scenario: Sign-off is recorded
  Then the CDO (or delegate), the a11y specialist and the FE lead have each recorded sign-off on the ticket, and the artefact links are added to the SCR-034/035/036 entries
```

title: Resolve O4: where each v1 indicator is computed (worker vs backend)
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` open question **O4** is still open: "Whether indicator computation belongs in the engine worker or the backend for heavy indicators". The doc already fixes the constraint - the rule engine runs server-side and must never depend on a browser, so **any indicator referenced by a rule IR is computed authoritatively in the backend** and the worker's copy is a display-only mirror that must reproduce it bit-for-bit (§14 parity test). O4 therefore only decides where *chart-only* indicators run. E13 cannot start T01/T02 without that decision, because it sets the `IndicatorDescriptor.compute` value (`client_worker` | `server`) for all ~28 v1 indicators and the shape of the parity test. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` schedules this at milestone M5; E13 is where it lands.

## Question(s) to answer
1. For each v1 indicator, is the worker able to compute it over a 100k-bar model, incrementally per closed bar, within the §4.3 allocation (<=2 ms/frame for indicator pane redraw, and <=250 ms for the first visible window on add)?
2. Which v1 indicators are rule-eligible today (per the `MetricRegistry` catalogue in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2: `atr`, `ema`, `sma`, `rsi`, `adx`, `swing_high`/`swing_low`, `cvd`, `delta`, volatility family) and therefore forced to `compute: server`?
3. Can a Python (`numpy`/`Decimal`-boundary) kernel and a TypeScript worker mirror agree bit-for-bit, or only to a stated epsilon? If only to an epsilon, what epsilon, and what does the parity test assert?
4. What is the cost of the mirror approach at ten active indicators - CPU in the worker, memory against the <=8 MB "profile/indicators/drawings" allocation in the engine memory table?

## Timebox
3 working days, agreed with the Architect. Not production code: a throwaway branch `spike/e13-indicator-compute` with a benchmark harness.

## Decision criteria (set before starting)
- If a worker implementation of the whole v1 set holds <=2 ms/frame and <=250 ms first-window at 100k bars, chart-only indicators default to `client_worker`.
- If any indicator exceeds it, that indicator is `server` and is delivered over the existing market-data WS as a derived series.
- If bit-for-bit parity is unachievable for the float-valued indicators, the parity test asserts `abs(a-b) <= 1e-8 * max(1, abs(a))` and the ADR records that this replaces "bit-for-bit" wording in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §14.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype worker kernel for the three worst cases (Ichimoku, MACD over a densified gapped series, VWAP with 3 sigma envelopes) plus one trivial case (SMA) as a control.
- Prototype Python kernel for the same four, in `services/api/orderflow/` spike form.
- Benchmark table: full compute and incremental update cost at 1k / 10k / 100k bars, worker CPU, memory delta.
- Parity table: max absolute and relative deviation per indicator over the recorded Bybit BTCUSDT fixture symbol-day.
- A `compute` assignment table for all ~28 v1 indicators, which becomes the seed data for `GET /api/v1/indicators`.

title: Black-box test plan for the indicator framework and v1 set
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires a QA-executed black-box test plan per Story before Done. E13 ships eight stories across three screens, ~28 indicators and a metric-exposure contract; a per-story ad hoc pass would miss the cross-cutting cases (value identity, provisional swings, partial history, ten-indicator load). This ticket writes the plan once, structured by story group, so execution is repeatable and traceable.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Test plan document `qa/plans/e13-indicators.md` with sections per story group: framework/UI (US-IND-001), MA family (US-IND-002), oscillators & sub-panes (US-IND-003), volatility & bands (US-IND-004), trend tools (US-IND-005), volume-based (US-IND-006), VWAP (US-IND-007), metric exposure (US-IND-008).
- Per section: preconditions, fixtures used, step-by-step cases covering happy path, each documented edge case and each failure mode, and expected results phrased so a pass/fail is unambiguous.
- A traceability table mapping every Gherkin scenario in the eight stories to at least one test case id, so gaps are visible rather than assumed away.
- Cross-cutting case set that no single story owns:
  - value identity (legend value == metric registry value == backend kernel value) for ATR, EMA and CVD;
  - a provisional Zig Zag swing is never selectable in an alert/rule picker;
  - partial CVD history on a symbol whose recording started mid-day;
  - ten indicators across three panes (frame budget, legend overflow, chip overflow);
  - preset save/apply/import round-trip including a hostile `WorkspaceBundle` payload;
  - symbol and timeframe switch with a full indicator stack loaded;
  - offline/backend-unreachable behaviour of SCR-034 and of `compute: server` indicators.
- Test data definition: which recorded Bybit fixture symbol-days are used (a normal day, a gap day, a partial-recording day) and how to load them.

## Out of scope
- Automated E2E implementation (E13-Q02), performance scripts (E13-Q03), the a11y audit (E13-Q04) and the parity regression pack (E13-Q05) - this plan references them rather than duplicating them.
- Exploratory charters (E13-Q06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every acceptance scenario is covered
  When the traceability table is reviewed against docs/plan/11-user-stories.md §7
  Then every Gherkin scenario in US-IND-001..008 maps to at least one test case, and any deliberate gap is listed with a reason and an owner

Scenario: A case is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer unfamiliar with E13 picks any case
  Then preconditions, fixture, steps and expected result are sufficient to execute and judge it without asking a developer

Scenario: Failure modes are first-class
  Then each story section contains at least one failure case (catalogue fetch failure, insufficient history, unrecorded symbol, blocked removal, invalid parameter) with its expected user-visible behaviour

Scenario: The plan is versioned with the feature
  Given a story's acceptance criteria change during implementation
  Then the plan is updated in the same PR cycle and the traceability table stays green
```

## Technical notes / design
The plan follows the structure in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` for black-box plans and reuses the fixture naming convention from the R1 integration suite so QA and engineering point at the same data. Cases are numbered `E13-TC-nnn` and referenced by the E2E tests in E13-Q02 so automation and manual execution share ids.

## Test plan
Self-referential: the plan is dry-run against an early build of E13-S01/S02 to confirm the cases are executable, and revised before the bulk of execution.

## Security notes
The plan includes the abuse-adjacent black-box cases from E13-X01 that do not need a security engineer to execute: cross-user preset access via the UI, hostile bundle import, and an out-of-range parameter entered directly.

## Accessibility notes
The plan references the E13-D05 accessibility acceptance script rather than restating it, so there is one script and it cannot drift.

## Performance notes
The ten-indicator case in the plan states the expected fps floor (>=55 fps per US-IND-001 NFR) and how to observe it, so manual execution can flag a regression before the automated benchmark run.

## Observability
Cases state which analytics/metric events should be emitted (`indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total`) so missing telemetry is caught as a defect.

title: Playwright E2E suite additions for indicators (web and Electron)
body:
## Context
R1's quality gate (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4) requires Playwright coverage in **both** web and Electron of: "load chart, switch symbol/timeframe, **add an indicator**, draw and persist a drawing, save and restore a workspace". This ticket owns the indicator portion of that suite and extends it to the E13-specific flows that the gate does not spell out but the stories require.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New specs under `tests/e2e/indicators/` running in both the web and Electron Playwright projects:
  1. `add-configure-remove.spec` - US-IND-001's three scenarios plus undo of removal and "add second instance".
  2. `subpane-lifecycle.spec` - add RSI, verify guide levels, resize the pane, reload, verify persisted height, remove the last indicator, verify collapse and space redistribution.
  3. `preset-roundtrip.spec` - save a preset from SCR-035, apply it on a new chart, edit it, delete it; verify built-ins are offered and immutable.
  4. `metric-exposure.spec` - add EMA(21) on a 5m chart, confirm `ema(21, 5m)` appears in the alert picker with a current value, create an alert, attempt removal, verify the block lists the referencing alert, disarm from the dialog, remove successfully.
  5. `object-tree-keyboard.spec` - complete a full add/configure/reorder/hide/remove cycle on SCR-036 without a mouse.
  6. `resilience.spec` - catalogue endpoint failure, backend unreachable while a `compute: server` indicator is active, symbol/timeframe switch with a full stack loaded.
- Page objects for SCR-034/035/036 and a seeded indicator-stack fixture reusable by E13-D07 and E13-Q03.
- Deterministic test data: fixed recorded fixture symbol-day loaded through the existing R1 fixture harness, and a frozen clock so value assertions are stable.
- Each spec tagged with the `E13-TC-nnn` ids from E13-Q01 so manual and automated coverage reconcile.

## Out of scope
- Value-correctness assertions at 1e-8 (that is unit/parity territory, E13-Q05) - E2E asserts presence, wiring and user-visible behaviour, not numerics.
- Performance measurement (E13-Q03) and the a11y audit (E13-Q04), though the keyboard spec overlaps deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The R1 gate case passes in both surfaces
  When the suite runs in the web and Electron Playwright projects
  Then "add an indicator" passes in both, as required by the R1 quality gate

Scenario: The suite is not flaky
  Given the suite runs 10 consecutive times in CI
  Then it passes every time with no retries required, or any flake is fixed rather than retried away

Scenario: A regression is caught
  Given a deliberate regression is introduced (sub-pane does not collapse on last-indicator removal)
  Then the suite fails with a message naming the scenario, verified by a mutation check before merge

Scenario: Failure paths are exercised
  Given the catalogue endpoint is stubbed to fail
  Then the suite asserts the SCR-034 error state with retry and that already-added indicators keep rendering
```

## Technical notes / design
Specs use the frozen-clock and fixture-replay harness from the R1 integration setup so live market movement cannot make an assertion flaky. Selectors use accessible roles and names (which doubles as a check that the a11y naming exists) rather than test ids where a role/name is available. Electron runs through the same page objects via the `_electron` fixture.

## Test plan
Self-testing: each spec is validated by a deliberate mutation before merge (the mutation check is part of the AC). CI runtime budget: the indicator suite must add <=4 minutes to the E2E stage; anything slower is split or moved to a nightly project.

## Security notes
The suite includes a negative case where a preset request is made as a second user and must fail - a cheap regression net for the object-level authorization control from E13-T03.

## Accessibility notes
`object-tree-keyboard.spec` is the automated backbone of the R1 exit criterion that "every chart is operable without a mouse"; it complements, and does not replace, the manual screen-reader pass in E13-Q04.

## Performance notes
E2E asserts responsiveness qualitatively only (an action completes without a timeout); numeric budgets belong to E13-Q03.

## Observability
The suite asserts that `indicator.added` / `indicator.removed` analytics events fire, so telemetry regressions are caught by the same run.

- [ ] Test artefacts committed to the repo and wired into CI where automatable.
- [ ] Executed at least once against a build; results recorded on the ticket with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Defects filed with repro steps, severity, environment and the failing scenario linked.
- [ ] Reviewed by the SDET lead; coverage of the story's acceptance criteria demonstrated by a traceability table.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted.

E13-S01 (surfaces), E13-S03 (sub-panes), E13-S08 (metric exposure and the removal guard). Uses E13-Q01's case ids.

title: Indicator performance benchmark and CI regression gate
body:
## Context
R1 exit criterion 1 requires "benchmark harness reports p95 <=16.6 ms with 100k bars + **all R1 overlays** on reference hardware in Electron; regressions >10% fail the build", and US-IND-001's NFR sets a specific indicator target: "adding 10 indicators must not reduce frame rate below 55 fps". The E11 benchmark harness exists; this ticket adds the indicator scenarios to it and wires them as a required check so an indicator change cannot quietly eat the frame budget.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New benchmark scenarios in the E11 harness:
  - **I1**: 100k bars + 10 indicators (mixed overlay and sub-pane, including the two heaviest: Ichimoku and VWAP with 3 envelopes) - asserts p95 frame <=16.6 ms and >=55 fps.
  - **I2**: indicator add latency - time from the SCR-034 add action to first paint of the visible window, asserts <=250 ms at 100k bars.
  - **I3**: parameter re-tune latency - time from a parameter change to visible-window repaint, asserts <=100 ms.
  - **I4**: worst-case degradation - the §4.2 stress scene with indicators active, asserts the 30 fps floor holds and that the degradation ladder coalesces indicator redraws to every second frame rather than dropping values.
  - **I5**: backend kernel throughput - per-bar incremental update for the full v1 set on one symbol, asserted within the backend-internal fan-out envelope (<=20 ms p95, budget #6).
  - **I6**: memory - indicator buffers stay within the <=8 MB "profile / indicators / drawings" allocation from the engine memory table at 10 instances over 100k bars.
- Seeded synthetic dataset reused from the E11 harness so results are comparable across trains; reference-hardware definition per `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.2.
- CI wiring: the indicator scenarios join the existing engine benchmark required check; a >10% regression against the stored baseline fails the build, with the baseline stored and updated through an explicit, reviewed commit.
- A results record committed to `docs/plan/benchmarks/e13-indicators.md` (first run) so E46 performance hardening has a baseline.

## Out of scope
- Backend load testing of WS fan-out (E17/Q tickets) and ingestion soak (E16) - I5 only measures the kernel's own cost.
- Optimising anything the benchmark finds - findings are filed as tickets against the owning story.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ten-indicator scene holds the budget
  When scenario I1 runs on reference hardware in Electron
  Then p95 frame time is <=16.6 ms and the measured frame rate is >=55 fps, and the numbers are recorded

Scenario: A regression fails the build
  Given a change increases I1's p95 frame time by more than 10% against the baseline
  Then the required CI check fails and names the scenario and the delta

Scenario: Degradation is verified, not assumed
  When scenario I4 runs
  Then the 30 fps floor holds, indicator redraws are observed to coalesce to every second frame, and no indicator value is missing or stale beyond the coalescing interval

Scenario: The kernel is measured separately from the renderer
  When scenario I5 runs
  Then the backend per-bar update cost for the full v1 set is reported independently of any frontend cost and compared against budget #6
```

## Technical notes / design
Measurement method per `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7: warm-up frames discarded, p50/p95/p99 reported, at least N=600 frames per scenario, run on the pinned reference machine profile. Benchmarks must be deterministic - the seeded dataset and a fixed indicator stack, no network. The E13-K01 prototype harness is promoted here rather than rewritten.

## Test plan
The benchmark is itself validated by injecting a known 20% slowdown and confirming the gate fires; the baseline file is reviewed by the chart-engine lead.

## Security notes
N/A. (Note only: a `compute: server` indicator's cost measured in I5 is the input to the rate/instance caps proposed by E13-X01.)

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance artefact. Its outputs feed R1 exit criterion 1 and the PRR performance evidence pack.

## Observability
The harness emits the same metric names the production code does (`indicator_compute_seconds`), so a benchmark result and a production metric are directly comparable.

title: Accessibility audit of the indicator surfaces (axe-core plus manual SR pass)
body:
## Context
R1 exit criterion 9 requires that "every chart is operable without a mouse" and R1's a11y gate requires "axe-core zero violations on all R1 routes; manual NVDA + VoiceOver pass on chart and drawing flows". SCR-036 is the designated accessible equivalent for canvas objects, so if it fails, the chart's a11y story fails with it. This audit executes the E13-D05 acceptance script against the built product.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core runs wired into CI for SCR-034, SCR-035 and SCR-036 in all their states (empty, populated, error, validation error, blocked removal), light and dark themes.
- Manual **NVDA** (Windows/Electron) and **VoiceOver** (macOS/web) passes executing the E13-D05 script: add an indicator, change a parameter, toggle visibility, reorder, remove, and read a legend value at a focused bar via the keyboard data cursor.
- Keyboard-only traversal audit: focus order, focus visibility, focus return on dialog close, no keyboard traps, the drag-reorder keyboard alternative, and sub-pane resize by keyboard.
- Colour-independence audit of the built UI: greyscale and deuteranopia/protanopia simulation of a ten-indicator scene, verifying dash patterns, glyphs and text labels carry every state (provisional, errored, warming up, hidden, locked, volume up/down).
- Contrast measurement of built styles (not just design frames), including band fills over dense candles.
- Announcement-cadence check: a fast-updating legend value must not flood the screen reader; verify the throttle specified in E13-D05.
- Findings report with WCAG 2.2 AA criterion references and severity; defects filed with `a11y` label.

## Out of scope
- The engine's DOM-mirror layer implementation (E11) - failures found there are filed against E11.
- Drawing tools (E14) and layouts (E15) a11y audits.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Zero automated violations
  When axe-core runs against SCR-034, SCR-035 and SCR-036 in every enumerated state and both themes
  Then zero violations are reported, and the checks are part of the CI a11y job

Scenario: A screen reader can complete the whole journey
  Given NVDA and separately VoiceOver
  Then a user can add, configure, reorder, hide and remove an indicator and read its value at a chosen bar, with every control announced by a meaningful name and state

Scenario: No state is colour-only
  When the ten-indicator scene is viewed in greyscale and under CVD simulation
  Then provisional, errored, warming-up, hidden, locked and volume up/down states are all still identifiable

Scenario: The screen reader is not flooded
  Given a fast-updating indicator value in the legend
  Then announcements respect the specified throttle and the user can still navigate away mid-update

Scenario: A blocking violation stops the epic
  Given a Critical or Serious violation is found
  Then E13 cannot reach Done until it is fixed or an Owner-approved, time-boxed exception is recorded
```

## Technical notes / design
Criteria applied per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. axe-core runs against the same Playwright page objects as E13-Q02, so the two suites share setup. Manual passes are scripted from E13-D05 so design intent and QA verification cannot diverge.

## Test plan

title: Parity and fixture regression pack for indicator values
body:
## Context
R1's integration gate requires that "bar builders and indicators [are] verified against recorded Bybit fixtures (a fixed, version-controlled symbol-day)", and `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §14 requires a parity test between the backend kernel and the worker mirror. US-IND-002 requires values matching reference implementations to 1e-8. This ticket builds the permanent regression pack that enforces all three at once, for every v1 indicator, so a refactor in R2 (when order-flow indicators join the same kernel) cannot silently change a number.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Golden-vector corpus in `tests/fixtures/indicators/`: for each v1 indicator and each of a small parameter matrix, input bars plus expected outputs, generated from an independent reference implementation and reviewed rather than self-generated from the code under test.
- Three fixture symbol-days from the recorded Bybit BTCUSDT set: a normal day, a day containing a gap (exercising `densify()`), and a day whose recording starts mid-session (exercising partial history).
- **Parity runner**: executes the Python kernel and the TypeScript worker mirror over the same inputs and asserts agreement within the tolerance fixed by E13-K01 (bit-for-bit or the recorded epsilon), reporting per-indicator worst-case deviation.
- **Reference-implementation cross-check**: each indicator compared to an independent reference to 1e-8 (US-IND-002 AC), with the specific discriminating cases pinned: EMA seeding, Wilder vs EMA smoothing (ATR/ADX/RSI/SMMA), population vs sample stdev (Bollinger), volume-weighted vs simple stdev (VWAP envelopes), PSAR acceleration, Ichimoku displacement, delta from aggression side (not candle direction).
- **Property-based suite**: incremental equals full for every plugin, over generated series including gaps, single-bar days, zero-volume bars and late amendments.
- Value-identity test: legend value == metric registry value == kernel value for ATR, EMA and CVD at a sampled set of bars.
- CI wiring: the pack is a required check; a deviation beyond tolerance fails the build naming the indicator and bar index.

## Out of scope
- Order-flow indicator parity (E18/E19/E23 add their own vectors to this same pack).
- Performance (E13-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every v1 indicator has golden vectors
  Then each of the ~28 v1 indicators has at least one golden-vector fixture per documented parameter variant, and the corpus is version-controlled

Scenario: Kernel and mirror agree
  When the parity runner executes over all three fixture days
  Then every indicator agrees within the E13-K01 tolerance, and the worst-case deviation per indicator is reported and recorded

Scenario: Reference agreement to 1e-8
  Then every indicator matches its independent reference implementation to 1e-8 on the fixture days, satisfying US-IND-002's acceptance criterion

Scenario: The discriminating cases actually discriminate
  Given a deliberate substitution of EMA smoothing for Wilder smoothing in ATR
  Then the pack fails, proving the fixture is sensitive to the error it exists to catch

Scenario: Late amendments are covered
  Given a late trade amends a closed bar on the fixture day
  Then affected indicator values are recomputed and the pack asserts the corrected series, not the stale one
```

## Technical notes / design
Golden vectors are generated once from an independent implementation (a well-known TA library or a hand-computed spreadsheet for the small cases) and then frozen - never regenerated from the code under test, which would make the test tautological. The fixture symbol-days are pinned by content hash so a storage change cannot silently alter them. The parity runner runs the TypeScript side under Node with the same worker code path the browser uses, not a re-implementation.

## Test plan
The pack is the test; it is itself validated by the mutation scenario in the AC (deliberate smoothing substitution must fail it). Runtime budget: <=3 minutes in CI; anything heavier moves to a nightly job with a daily report.

## Security notes
Fixtures contain public market data only - no keys, no account identifiers. Confirm this with a secrets scan over the fixture directory as part of the pack's own CI job.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Not a performance test, but the pack records per-indicator compute time as a side output so a pathological slowdown shows up even between E13-Q03 runs.

## Observability
On failure, the report names indicator, parameter set, fixture day, bar index, expected and actual - enough to debug without re-running locally.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed to the repo and wired into CI where automatable.
- [ ] Executed at least once against a build; results recorded on the ticket with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Defects filed with repro steps, severity, environment and the failing scenario linked.
- [ ] Reviewed by the SDET lead; coverage of the story's acceptance criteria demonstrated by a traceability table.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted.

## Dependencies
E13-S05, E13-S06, E13-S07 (the last indicators to land, so the corpus is complete); E13-K01 fixes the tolerance; E12 supplies the recorded fixture days.

title: Exploratory charters, chaos scenarios and E13 QA sign-off
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires an Epic-level regression and exploratory pass, "not just child-ticket QA", before an Epic can be Done. Scripted tests verify what was thought of; exploratory charters and chaos scenarios find what was not. This ticket closes E13 from a QA perspective.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (time-boxed, session-based, notes recorded per session):
  1. "Explore adding and removing indicators rapidly, with an emphasis on the undo stack and instance identity, to discover state corruption."
  2. "Explore parameter editing at the boundaries (1, 5000, non-integers, paste, rapid repeated edits) to discover validation and recompute defects."
  3. "Explore the SCR-036 object tree with a large mixed stack (indicators, drawings, alerts) to discover reorder/visibility/lock inconsistencies."
  4. "Explore indicator behaviour across symbol and timeframe switching, including switching mid-recompute, to discover stale-series defects."
  5. "Explore presets and workspace bundle import/export, including hand-edited payloads, to discover validation and trust defects."
  6. "Explore the interaction of indicators with bar types that have no fixed time width (renko, range) to discover disabled-indicator and tooltip defects."
- **Chaos scenarios** executed against a staging build:
  - backend unreachable while `compute: server` indicators are active - values must go stale-with-notice, never silently freeze at a last value presented as live;
  - WS resync mid-session - indicator series must reconcile without duplicated or missing bars;
  - a late-amended bar during active rendering;
  - worker crash/restart - indicators must re-register and recompute rather than leaving empty panes;
  - storage slow/unavailable during a historical backfill of a `compute: server` series.
- **Regression pack** addition: the E13 cases that must run in every future train's regression sweep, added to the shared regression suite with their `E13-TC-nnn` ids.
- **Epic QA sign-off**: a consolidated report with pass/fail per story, open defects by severity, and an explicit statement that zero P0/P1 defects remain open against E13 scope (R1 exit criterion 10).

## Out of scope
- Fixing defects found (filed against the owning story or as new Bugs).
- Load testing of the WS fan-out path (E17).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Charters are executed and recorded
  Then each of the six charters has a recorded session with duration, areas covered, defects found and a coverage judgement, per the session-based testing format in docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md

Scenario: Stale is never presented as live
  Given the backend becomes unreachable while a compute:server indicator is active
  Then the indicator's value is marked stale in text and the legend states the staleness, rather than continuing to display the last value as current

Scenario: A worker restart recovers
  Given the engine worker is killed mid-session
  Then all indicator instances re-register and recompute, the panes repopulate, and no instance loses its palette slot or metric key

Scenario: Sign-off is evidence-based
  Then the sign-off report lists every story with pass/fail per acceptance scenario, enumerates open defects by severity, and states that no P0/P1 defect remains open against E13

Scenario: Regression cases are handed forward
  Then the agreed E13 cases are present in the shared regression suite and run in the next train's sweep
```

## Technical notes / design
Chaos is induced with the same fault-injection tooling the R1 chaos work uses (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018) extended with a worker-kill and a backend-unreachable toggle. Sessions follow session-based test management: charter, time box, notes, defects, coverage judgement.

## Test plan
Self-evident (this ticket is test execution). Quality control: a second QA reviews the charter notes for coverage gaps before sign-off.

## Security notes
Charter 5 (hand-edited preset/bundle payloads) doubles as the black-box half of the E13-X01 abuse cases; findings are shared with the Security engineer for E13-X02.

## Accessibility notes
At least one charter session is run keyboard-only and one with a screen reader active, so exploratory coverage is not sighted-mouse-only.

## Performance notes
Chaos scenarios are observed for frame-budget impact: a resync or worker restart must not leave the scene below the 30 fps floor once recovered.

## Observability
Verify that every chaos scenario produces the expected telemetry (stale markers, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, worker restart log) - missing telemetry during an incident is itself a defect.

title: Add, configure and remove indicators from the chart
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-001** (Must): "As a trader, I want to add indicators with editable parameters and styles, so that my chart reflects my method." This is the shell every other IND story plugs into - without it the v1 indicator set has no way onto a chart. It builds the three catalogued screens SCR-034 (indicator library), SCR-035 (indicator settings dialog) and SCR-036 (indicator manager / object tree), against the E13-D06 handoff pack.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-034 Indicator library** (`apps/web/src/features/indicators/`): modal rendering the catalogue from `GET /api/v1/indicators`, grouped Overlay / Sub-pane / Order-flow, fuzzy search (CMP-054 SearchBox + CMP-213 FuzzyList), category tabs (CMP-042), per-entry card (CMP-050) with preview thumbnail, "requires recorded history" marking for `compute: server` descriptors, empty-search state (CMP-026), favourites/recents from `indicator_presets.is_favourite`, and the "already present - add second instance" affordance.
- **SCR-035 Indicator settings dialog**: Inputs / Style / Visibility / Scale / Alerts tabs; the Inputs form is generated from the descriptor's `params_schema` (CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-065 FormSection); Style tab binds `color.indicator.palette[]` tokens and dash patterns via CMP-031 ColorSwatch; Scale tab offers own scale / merged / pinned right; live preview (CMP-228 PreviewTile); validation "Period must be between 1 and 5000."; "save as default for this indicator" writing an `indicator_presets` row; reset; Alerts tab links to SCR-091.
- **SCR-036 Indicator manager**: drawer (CMP-046) with `role="tree"` over panes -> indicators -> drawings -> alerts; per-item visibility, lock, rename, reorder (drag plus keyboard alternative) and delete; multi-select and bulk actions; empty state.
- **Legend and chips**: CMP-199 ChartLegend entries and the CMP-224 IndicatorChips row with current value, visibility toggle, settings and remove, each a separately named button.
- Wiring to the E13-T01 runtime: add -> `addIndicator(plugin, params)`, parameter change -> `recompute(range)`, remove -> disposal; undo for removal per US-IND-001.
- Preset consumption: apply a preset on add; "save as default"; built-in presets from §10.5 offered first.

## Out of scope
- The indicator implementations themselves (E13-S02..S07) - this story ships with SMA/EMA from S02 as the smoke case and the rest arrive behind it.
- Alert editor internals (E40); chart templates and layout persistence of the stack (E15); the metric-in-use removal guard (E13-S08 adds the blocking behaviour on top of this story's removal flow).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Add
  When I add EMA(21) from the indicator picker
  Then it renders in the price pane with a legend entry showing the parameter and current value

Scenario: Reconfigure
  Given EMA(21) is on the chart
  When I change the length to 34
  Then the series recomputes incrementally and the legend updates without a chart reload, and the visible window repaints within 100 ms

Scenario: Remove
  When I remove it
  Then it disappears from the pane, the legend and the template diff, with undo available

Scenario: Second instance
  Given EMA(21) is already present
  When I add EMA from the library again
  Then I am offered "Add second instance", the new instance takes the next palette slot, and the two legend entries are distinguishable by parameters and colour

Scenario: The catalogue cannot be loaded
  Given GET /api/v1/indicators fails
  Then SCR-034 shows an error state with a retry action, no partial list is presented as complete, and previously added indicators keep rendering

Scenario: Ten indicators keep the frame budget
  Given ten indicators are active
  Then the engine benchmark reports >=55 fps and no frame exceeds the 30 fps floor

Scenario: Keyboard only
  Given I never touch the mouse
  Then I can open the library, search, add an indicator, open its settings, change a parameter, toggle visibility, reorder it and remove it, with focus always visible and returned to a sensible element on dialog close
```

## Technical notes / design
Form generation: the Inputs tab is a JSON-Schema-driven renderer restricted to an enumerated control set (number, integer, enum select, boolean, colour token, source-series select). It must never render free-form HTML or markdown - the schema is server-authored but the renderer stays conservative so the seam cannot become an injection vector. Parameter edits are debounced (the spec value from E13-D04) and recompute the visible window first, then backfill off-screen ranges in the worker. Instance identity uses the stable key from E13-T01 (`sha1(indicatorId + canonical(params) + sourceSeriesId)`), so a reload restores the same key, the same palette slot and the same metric name. Removal emits an undoable command onto the chart's command stack.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): schema-driven form rendering for each control type, validation messages, preset application, undo of removal, palette-slot assignment determinism. Integration: add/configure/remove against a stubbed engine; catalogue fetch failure; preset save round-trip. E2E (Playwright, web and Electron): the US-IND-001 three scenarios plus second-instance and keyboard-only paths. Perf: the ten-indicator benchmark (harness owned by E13-Q03). A11y: axe-core on all three screens; NVDA spot check of the tree. Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model. Additionally: the settings form must treat `params_schema` as data, not code - no `eval`, no dynamic component resolution by name from the payload. Preset writes go through the T03 endpoints which enforce owner scope, so the UI never assumes client-side authorization.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-036 is the designated accessible equivalent for canvas objects and must satisfy the full keyboard contract from E13-D05: arrow navigation in the tree, Enter to open settings, Space to toggle visibility, Delete to remove, and a documented keyboard alternative to drag-reorder. SCR-034's list is a listbox whose entries announce their pane target. SCR-035's colour pickers expose token names. Series must be distinguishable without colour: each gets a distinct dash pattern from the E13-D04 ladder. State (warming up, provisional, errored) is stated in text in the legend, never by colour alone. Legend values and per-instance names are published into the E11 DOM-mirror layer with the announcement cadence set by E13-D05. Every control introduced is reachable and operable from SCR-036.

## Performance notes
Budgets: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars (SCR-034); parameter re-tune of the visible window <=100 ms (SCR-035); ten active indicators must not drop the scene below 55 fps (US-IND-001 NFR) and never below the 30 fps floor (budget #2). SCR-036 tree operations are O(1) against the render list and never force a full chart rebuild (catalogue requirement).

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}` (ERROR log with both values and bar index on any mismatch), `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`; analytics `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`. SCR-036 additionally emits `indicator.reordered` and `indicator.visibility_toggled`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass via automated tests that name the scenario.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% on `packages/chart-engine` / `services/api/orderflow`, >=80% on `apps/web` for new/changed lines.

- [ ] perf: engine benchmark re-run, no >10% regression against budget #1; the story's own budget measured.
- [ ] design-qa: compared against the E13-D03/D04 spec; discrepancies fixed or filed as Bugs.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario; demoed at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via merge queue, 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; feature-flag state recorded.

## Dependencies
E13-T01 (runtime), E13-T02 (catalogue endpoint + descriptors), E13-T03 (presets), E13-D06 (signed-off design, required by the design-ahead rule). E11 supplies panes, legend and the a11y mirror; E05 supplies the dialog/drawer primitives.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). The first consuming frontend stories (E13-S01, E13-S02) start in **Sprint 07**, which is **2 full sprints** after design Done, so the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule is satisfied on its own terms and **no Architect/CDO waiver is required** for E13-S01, E13-S02, E13-S03, E13-S04, E13-S06, E13-S07 or E13-S08. Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.
## Branch
`feat/e13-indicators-ui`; split as library modal / settings dialog / object tree to keep each PR <=400 LOC.

title: Moving-average family indicators (SMA, EMA, WMA, VWMA, SMMA, DEMA, TEMA, ribbon)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-002** (Must for SMA/EMA, Should for WMA/VWMA/SMMA/DEMA/TEMA and the MA ribbon/cross). Its NFR is the epic's central constraint: "shared indicator kernel used by chart, alerts, rule engine and backtest - one implementation, one result." `ema` and `sma` are already named metrics in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2, so this story extends the existing registry entries rather than creating parallel ones. It is also the first real exercise of the E13-T01/T02 seam, which is why it lands before the other indicator stories.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Worker plugins and backend kernel functions for `sma`, `ema`, `wma`, `vwma`, `smma` (Wilder/running MA), `dema`, `tema`, each with `length` and `source` (`close` | `open` | `high` | `low` | `hl2` | `hlc3` | `ohlc4`) parameters and an `offset` parameter.
- **MA ribbon**: one instance producing N output series (default 5 lengths) rendered as a single legend entry with an expandable list (CMP-199 variant from E13-D04).
- **MA cross**: a derived boolean/marker output (fast crosses slow) exposed as a metric so alerts and rules can reference it.
- `MetricDescriptor` registration for each: unit `price`, value_type `number`, inputs `bars`, cadence `on_bar_close`, confidence `exact`, `warmup_bars = length` (and the composed warmup for DEMA/TEMA), `nullable_when` stating exactly when the value is None.
- Golden-vector fixtures per MA type over the recorded Bybit BTCUSDT fixture symbol-day, including a day with a gap so densification is exercised.
- Insufficient-history behaviour: render from the first valid bar and state in the legend how many more bars are needed.

## Out of scope
- Oscillators (S03), bands (S04), trend tools (S05), volume-based (S06), VWAP (S07) - VWAP is its own story because it shares the anchored-VWAP drawing kernel.
- Alert/rule editor UI; the metric exposure *guarantees* are S08.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: SMA/EMA
  Given the recorded fixture symbol-day
  Then values match reference implementations to 1e-8 on the test fixtures, for both the backend kernel and the worker mirror

Scenario: Ribbon
  When I add an MA ribbon of 5 lengths
  Then it renders as one legend entry with an expandable list, and the five series are distinguishable without colour

Scenario: Insufficient history
  Given fewer bars than the period exist
  Then the indicator renders only from the first valid bar and states how many bars are still needed

Scenario: Source selection changes the result
  Given SMA(20) on close and a second instance on hl2
  Then the two instances produce different series, carry different metric keys, and are separately labelled in the legend

Scenario: Incremental equals full
  Given any MA type over a generated 100k-bar series
  When the series is built by appending bars one at a time
  Then every value equals the full recomputation, asserted by a property-based test
```

## Technical notes / design
Each indicator is a plugin against the E13-T01 `IndicatorPlugin` interface (<=150 lines per `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12) and a matching `MetricDescriptor` registration in the E13-T02 backend kernel (M9). The two implementations are held together by shared golden-vector fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/` and the parity assertion established by E13-K01. Unit: golden vectors per MA type and per source; EMA seeding; SMMA-vs-EMA discrimination; DEMA/TEMA warmup; VWMA zero-volume rule. Integration: ribbon rendering with five outputs from one instance. Coverage >=85% engine/backend.

Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model.

Legend values and per-instance names are published into the E11 DOM-mirror layer with the announcement cadence set by E13-D05. Every control introduced is reachable and operable from SCR-036.
