title: Oscillators in linked sub-panes (RSI, MACD, Stochastic, CCI, Williams %R)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-003** (Must for RSI and MACD, Should for Stochastic/CCI/Williams %R). This is the story that introduces **sub-pane lifecycle** to the product: creating a linked sub-pane with its own scale and guide levels, sharing the crosshair, persisting pane heights per layout, and collapsing the pane when its last indicator is removed. That lifecycle is why this story is larger than the other indicator-set stories and why E15 (layouts) depends on E13.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Plugins + kernel functions for `rsi` (Wilder), `macd` (fast/slow/signal with line, signal and histogram outputs), `stochastic` (%K/%D with smoothing), `cci`, `williams_r`.
- **Sub-pane lifecycle** in `packages/chart-engine` + `apps/web`: adding a `pane: sub` indicator creates a linked sub-pane with its own price scale, guide levels (30/70 for RSI, zero line for MACD, 20/80 for Stochastic), shared crosshair and synced time axis; adding a second sub-pane indicator of the same id targets the existing pane or a new one per the user's choice; removing the last indicator in a sub-pane collapses it and redistributes vertical space per the E13-D04 motion spec.
- Sub-pane heights persisted per layout (US-IND-003 NFR) - the persistence contract E15 consumes; E13 writes the values, E15 owns the workspace envelope.
- **Divergence marking**: confirmed RSI/MACD divergences marked with a glyph plus a text label, never colour alone; a `*_divergence` metric registered with `confidence="estimated"` consistent with `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2 (`delta_divergence`, `cvd_divergence` are already `estimated`).
- `MetricDescriptor` registration for each oscillator, with `unit` (`ratio` for RSI/Stochastic, `price` for MACD line, `zscore`-like for CCI) and warmup declared.

## Out of scope
- Order-flow sub-panes (CVD pane E23, OI/funding E24) - they reuse this lifecycle.
- Workspace/layout persistence itself (E15) beyond emitting the pane-height values.
- Divergence-based rules (E35) - only the metric is published here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sub-pane
  When I add RSI(14)
  Then a linked sub-pane is created with its own scale, guide levels at 30/70 and shared crosshair

Scenario: Divergence marking
  Given RSI divergence detection is enabled
  Then confirmed divergences are marked with a glyph plus a text label, never colour alone

Scenario: Pane management
  When I remove the last indicator in a sub-pane
  Then the sub-pane collapses and vertical space redistributes

Scenario: Heights persist
  Given I resize the RSI sub-pane and reload the app
  Then the sub-pane returns at the same height for that layout

Scenario: MACD emits three outputs into one pane
  When I add MACD(12,26,9)
  Then line, signal and histogram render in one sub-pane under one legend entry with all three current values readable

Scenario: Many sub-panes degrade gracefully
  Given four sub-pane indicators are active alongside the price pane
  Then the price pane retains at least the minimum height from the design spec, and the frame budget still holds at >=55 fps
```

## Technical notes / design
Each indicator is a plugin against the E13-T01 `IndicatorPlugin` interface (<=150 lines per `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12) and a matching `MetricDescriptor` registration in the E13-T02 backend kernel (M9). The two implementations are held together by shared golden-vector fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/` and the parity assertion established by E13-K01. Every indicator declares `warmup_bars`; values before warmup are absent, never zero. No indicator reads wall-clock time. Styling comes from `color.indicator.palette[]` and the dash ladder defined by E13-D04 - never a hard-coded colour. RSI must use Wilder smoothing; a fixture discriminates it from a simple-average RSI. Divergence detection is pivot-based with `pivot_lookback` and `n` parameters mirroring the existing `cvd_divergence` descriptor so the vocabulary stays consistent; only *confirmed* pivots produce a marking - an unconfirmed pivot is never marked and never reaches a rule (the same discipline US-IND-005 imposes on ZigZag). Sub-pane height is stored as a ratio, not pixels, so it survives a window resize.

## Test plan
Unit: golden vectors for each oscillator; Wilder-RSI discrimination; MACD three-output alignment; divergence pivot confirmation logic including the "never mark an unconfirmed pivot" case. Integration: sub-pane create/collapse/redistribute; height persistence round-trip; crosshair sync across panes. E2E: add RSI, resize the pane, reload, confirm height; remove the last indicator and confirm collapse. Perf: four-sub-pane scene in the benchmark. A11y: sub-pane is announced with its name and value; divergence markers have text equivalents. Coverage >=85% engine/backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model. Sub-pane count is capped (design spec value) so a hostile or careless preset import cannot create unbounded panes.

## Accessibility notes
Series must be distinguishable without colour: each gets a distinct dash pattern from the E13-D04 ladder. State (warming up, provisional, errored) is stated in text in the legend, never by colour alone. Legend values and per-instance names are published into the E11 DOM-mirror layer with the announcement cadence set by E13-D05. Every control introduced is reachable and operable from SCR-036. Each sub-pane is a labelled region; the keyboard data cursor (E11) reads the oscillator value at the focused bar alongside OHLCV; pane resize has a keyboard alternative; divergence glyphs carry a text label per US-IND-003.

## Performance notes
Budgets: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars (SCR-034); parameter re-tune of the visible window <=100 ms (SCR-035); ten active indicators must not drop the scene below 55 fps (US-IND-001 NFR) and never below the 30 fps floor (budget #2). `indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}` (ERROR log with both values and bar index on any mismatch), `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`; analytics `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`. E13-S02 (kernel seam proven), E13-S01 (add/configure/remove UI exists to drive pane creation). E11 supplies multi-pane stacking with a synced time axis. Gates E15's layout persistence of pane heights.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). ## Context
Implements **US-IND-004** (Must for Bollinger Bands, ATR, ADX; Should for Keltner and Donchian). Its NFR - "ATR is exposed as a first-class metric to the rule DSL" - and its first scenario - "the same ATR value is available to the sizing calculator, the rule engine and alerts" - are exactly why the kernel is backend-authoritative. `atr` and `adx` already exist as metrics in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2 (Wilder ATR `n=14`; Wilder ADX `n=14`, trending >25, ranging <20), and per-account profiles already allow an `sl_offset_unit` of `"atr"` (§ profile schema), so a wrong ATR would silently mis-size stops. This story is therefore held to the strictest correctness bar in the epic.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Kernel + plugins for `atr` (Wilder), `adx` (Wilder, with +DI/-DI outputs), `bollinger` (length, multiplier; upper/middle/lower outputs plus optional shaded channel), `keltner` (EMA basis + ATR multiple), `donchian` (upper/lower/mid).
- Band rendering: shaded channel fill whose alpha is the E13-D04 value, verified to keep candle body/wick contrast at worst-case density (US-IND-004 scenario "keeps candle contrast").
- Parameter validation surfaced inline: entering a period of 0 shows an inline error and retains the previous value (US-IND-004 scenario), enforced both in the SCR-035 form and in the kernel.
- `MetricDescriptor` completeness for `atr`/`adx` including `unit` (`price` for ATR, `ratio` for ADX), `warmup_bars`, `cadence: on_bar_close`, `deterministic: true`, `confidence: exact`, and `nullable_when` text.
- An explicit shared-value test: the value the chart legend shows for ATR(14) at bar N equals the value the kernel serves to a metric consumer for the same `(symbol, bar_spec, params)` at bar N.

## Out of scope
- The sizing calculator, rule engine and alert consumers themselves (E28/E35/E40) - this story guarantees the value; E13-S08 guarantees the exposure contract.
- Regime classification (`market_regime`, `hurst`) - E25 in R2, though it consumes this ADX.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: ATR used elsewhere
  Given ATR(14) is configured
  Then the same value is available to the sizing calculator, the rule engine and alerts, asserted by a test that reads the metric registry and the chart legend and compares them

Scenario: Bands render
  When I add Bollinger(20,2)
  Then upper/middle/lower render with an optional shaded channel that keeps candle contrast, measured against the WCAG non-text contrast threshold at worst-case candle density

Scenario: Parameter validation
  When I enter a period of 0
  Then the field shows an inline error and the previous value is retained, and no request or recomputation is issued

Scenario: Wilder smoothing is used
  Given the recorded fixture symbol-day
  Then ATR and ADX match a Wilder reference to 1e-8 and are measurably different from an EMA-smoothed variant, asserted by a discriminating fixture

Scenario: Insufficient history
  Given fewer bars than the ADX warmup (2n) exist
  Then no ADX value is emitted, the legend states how many more bars are needed, and no zero is drawn
```

## Technical notes / design
Each indicator is a plugin against the E13-T01 `IndicatorPlugin` interface (<=150 lines per `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12) and a matching `MetricDescriptor` registration in the E13-T02 backend kernel (M9). The two implementations are held together by shared golden-vector fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/` and the parity assertion established by E13-K01. Every indicator declares `warmup_bars`; values before warmup are absent, never zero. No indicator reads wall-clock time. Styling comes from `color.indicator.palette[]` and the dash ladder defined by E13-D04 - never a hard-coded colour. ATR warmup is `n` with a Wilder seed of the simple average of the first `n` true ranges; ADX warmup is effectively `2n` because DX is itself smoothed - both are declared, not implied. True range must use the previous close including across a gap; the fixture includes a gap day precisely to pin this. Bollinger uses the population standard deviation (stated explicitly; the fixture discriminates population from sample).

## Test plan
Unit: golden vectors for all five; Wilder-vs-EMA discrimination for ATR and ADX; population-vs-sample stdev discrimination for Bollinger; true-range-across-gap case; period-0 rejection at kernel level. Property-based: incremental equals full. Parity: Python vs TypeScript within the K01 tolerance. Integration: the shared-value test comparing legend and metric registry. Contrast test: automated measurement of band fill over the densest candle fixture. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model. Elevated care: ATR feeds `sl_offset_unit="atr"` in per-account profiles, so an incorrect or manipulable ATR has a financial safety consequence. The kernel value is authoritative and server-side; the worker value is display-only and can never be the source for a stop offset. This constraint is asserted by a test and called out for the E13-X01 threat model.

## Accessibility notes
Series must be distinguishable without colour: each gets a distinct dash pattern from the E13-D04 ladder. State (warming up, provisional, errored) is stated in text in the legend, never by colour alone. Legend values and per-instance names are published into the E11 DOM-mirror layer with the announcement cadence set by E13-D05. Every control introduced is reachable and operable from SCR-036. The band fill must not reduce candle contrast below the non-text threshold; the middle band is distinguishable from the MA family by dash pattern.

## Performance notes
Budgets: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars (SCR-034); parameter re-tune of the visible window <=100 ms (SCR-035); ten active indicators must not drop the scene below 55 fps (US-IND-001 NFR) and never below the 30 fps floor (budget #2). A band indicator is three series plus a fill; it must remain within the instanced line + fill passes without adding a per-instance draw call beyond the budgeted <=40 for the combined scene.

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}` (ERROR log with both values and bar index on any mismatch), `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`; analytics `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`. An ATR parity mismatch is logged at ERROR and raises `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator="atr"}` - treated as a P1 defect because of the stop-sizing consequence.

- [ ] perf: engine benchmark re-run, no >10% regression against budget #1; the story's own budget measured.
- [ ] design-qa: compared against the E13-D03/D04 spec; discrepancies fixed or filed as Bugs.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario; demoed at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via merge queue, 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; feature-flag state recorded.

## Dependencies
E13-S02 (kernel seam), E13-T02 (registry). Feeds E28 (per-account profiles' ATR-based SL offsets), E35 (rules), E40 (alerts), E25 (regime).


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). The first consuming frontend stories (E13-S01, E13-S02) start in **Sprint 07**, which is **2 full sprints** after design Done, so the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule is satisfied on its own terms and **no Architect/CDO waiver is required** for E13-S01, E13-S02, E13-S03, E13-S04, E13-S06, E13-S07 or E13-S08. Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.

title: Trend tools: Supertrend, Zig Zag, Ichimoku and Parabolic SAR
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-005** (Must for Supertrend and Zig Zag; Should for Ichimoku and Parabolic SAR). This story carries the epic's sharpest safety rule, stated as the story's NFR: "no rule may act on a provisional swing - enforced in the rule engine, covered by tests." Zig Zag repaints by construction; publishing an unconfirmed swing as if it were settled would let a structure-based trailing stop act on a leg that later disappears. The story therefore ships both the indicators and the `provisional` contract that the rest of the platform relies on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Kernel + plugins for `supertrend` (ATR-based, period and multiplier; outputs the band and a direction enum), `zigzag` (deviation % and/or ATR-based, depth), `ichimoku` (tenkan/kijun/senkou A/B/chikou with the displacement rules), `psar` (step, max step).
- **Direction and flip rendering**: Supertrend direction flips render with a marker (CMP-195 AnnotationMarker) *and* a text label, and the current direction is stated in the legend.
- **Named swing metrics**: confirmed Zig Zag swing highs and lows exposed as named metrics usable by structure-based trailing stops, aligning with the existing `swing_high`/`swing_low` descriptors in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2.
- **Provisional contract**: the last, unconfirmed Zig Zag leg renders dashed with a "provisional" label, carries `provisional=true` on the output buffer channel from E13-T01, and is excluded from rule evaluation at the source - the kernel does not publish provisional values into the metric registry at all, so no downstream consumer can accidentally read one.
- Ichimoku displacement handling, including drawing the cloud into the future beyond the last bar without corrupting the time-scale's bar model.
- Descriptor registration with `confidence` set honestly: Supertrend/PSAR/Ichimoku are `exact` (deterministic formulas); the Zig Zag *provisional* leg is excluded rather than marked estimated, and any derived structure signal is `estimated`.

## Out of scope
- The rule engine's enforcement of the provisional rule (E35) - E13 provides the guarantee at the source and the test that proves it; E35 adds its own assertion.
- Structure-based trailing-stop behaviour itself (E32/E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Supertrend
  Then direction flips render with a marker and a text label, and the current direction is in the legend

Scenario: Zig Zag swings
  Then confirmed swing highs and lows are exposed as named metrics usable by structure-based trailing stops

Scenario: Repainting disclosure
  Given Zig Zag's last leg is unconfirmed
  Then it renders dashed with a "provisional" label and is excluded from rule evaluation

Scenario: A provisional swing can never be read by a consumer
  Given a metric consumer requests the latest swing_high while the last leg is unconfirmed
  Then the value returned is the last confirmed swing, never the provisional one, asserted by a test at the registry boundary

Scenario: Ichimoku projects forward
  When the cloud is displaced 26 bars ahead
  Then it renders beyond the last bar without extending the bar model, without shifting the price scale, and the crosshair over the projected region reads the cloud values with no OHLCV

Scenario: A confirmed swing is revised by a late amendment
  Given a late trade amends a closed bar that formed a confirmed pivot
  Then the affected legs are recomputed and republished, and any consumer is served the corrected value rather than the stale one
```

## Technical notes / design
Each indicator is a plugin against the E13-T01 `IndicatorPlugin` interface (<=150 lines per `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12) and a matching `MetricDescriptor` registration in the E13-T02 backend kernel (M9). The two implementations are held together by shared golden-vector fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/` and the parity assertion established by E13-K01. Every indicator declares `warmup_bars`; values before warmup are absent, never zero. No indicator reads wall-clock time. Styling comes from `color.indicator.palette[]` and the dash ladder defined by E13-D04 - never a hard-coded colour. Supertrend consumes the S04 `atr` kernel rather than reimplementing true range - one implementation, one result. Zig Zag confirmation: a pivot is confirmed once price has moved the deviation threshold in the opposite direction; until then the leg is provisional. PSAR's acceleration factor and reversal handling is pinned by a golden vector because naive implementations drift. Ichimoku's senkou displacement is a render-time offset, not synthetic bars appended to the `BarStore`.

## Test plan
Unit: golden vectors for all four; PSAR acceleration/reversal; Ichimoku displacement arithmetic; Zig Zag confirmation state machine including the provisional-to-confirmed transition and the re-provisionalisation after an amended bar. Boundary test: metric registry never returns a provisional value. Integration: late-amendment recompute; Ichimoku forward projection against the time scale. E2E: Supertrend flip marker and legend direction. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model. Safety-relevant: a provisional swing reaching a trailing-stop rule would move a real stop on false information. The mitigation is structural (not published at all, rather than published-with-a-flag) and is covered by an explicit test named in the AC. Flagged for the E13-X01 threat model as a tampering/integrity concern.

## Accessibility notes
Series must be distinguishable without colour: each gets a distinct dash pattern from the E13-D04 ladder. State (warming up, provisional, errored) is stated in text in the legend, never by colour alone. Legend values and per-instance names are published into the E11 DOM-mirror layer with the announcement cadence set by E13-D05. Every control introduced is reachable and operable from SCR-036. The provisional state is carried by a dash pattern *and* the word "provisional" in the legend and in the screen-reader announcement; Supertrend flips are a glyph plus a text label per US-IND-005; the Ichimoku cloud's two boundaries are distinguishable without colour.

## Performance notes
Budgets: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars (SCR-034); parameter re-tune of the visible window <=100 ms (SCR-035); ten active indicators must not drop the scene below 55 fps (US-IND-001 NFR) and never below the 30 fps floor (budget #2). Ichimoku is five series plus a filled cloud - the heaviest single v1 indicator and one of the E13-K01 prototyped worst cases; its measured cost must match the K01 prediction or the discrepancy is investigated before merge.

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}` (ERROR log with both values and bar index on any mismatch), `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`; analytics `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`. Plus `indicator_zigzag_reprovisionalised_total` so repaint churn is visible rather than anecdotal.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass via automated tests that name the scenario.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% on `packages/chart-engine` / `services/api/orderflow`, >=80% on `apps/web` for new/changed lines.
- [ ] Docs updated (`22-api-openapi.yaml` / `24-internal-schemas.md` / `14-screens-catalogue.md` as touched); changelog fragment added.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on touched screens; keyboard-only path verified; screen-reader spot check recorded.
- [ ] perf: engine benchmark re-run, no >10% regression against budget #1; the story's own budget measured.
- [ ] design-qa: compared against the E13-D03/D04 spec; discrepancies fixed or filed as Bugs.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario; demoed at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via merge queue, 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; feature-flag state recorded.

## Dependencies
E13-S04 (ATR kernel, consumed by Supertrend). E12's amended-bar path drives the re-confirmation case.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). The first consuming frontend stories (E13-S01, E13-S02) start in **Sprint 07**, which is **2 full sprints** after design Done, so the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule is satisfied on its own terms and **no Architect/CDO waiver is required** for E13-S01, E13-S02, E13-S03, E13-S04, E13-S06, E13-S07 or E13-S08. Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.

title: Volume indicators: histogram, volume MA, OBV and delta-aware colouring
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-006** (Must for the volume histogram and classic CVD; Should for OBV/CMF/MFI). Its NFR - "single delta computation shared with footprint, Deep-Stats and the CVD pane" - makes this story the place where the `delta`/`cvd` kernel is settled *before* R2 builds footprint (E18), Deep-Stats (E20) and the dedicated CVD pane (E23) on top of it. `delta` and `cvd` already exist as metrics in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2 (`cvd` with an `anchor` parameter of `session|utc_day|since_load|custom_ts`); this story registers the indicator forms over that same computation, it does not fork it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Volume histogram series with up/down encoding by **pattern and colour** (never colour alone), plus an optional average-volume line (`volume_ma`, configurable length).
- Classic **CVD indicator** form over the existing `cvd` metric with its `anchor` parameter; value identity with the future dedicated CVD pane is guaranteed by sharing the kernel, and asserted by a test fixture that the E23 story will reuse.
- `obv`, `cmf` (Chaikin Money Flow), `mfi` (Money Flow Index) kernel functions and plugins.
- **Partial-history handling**: where a requested range predates recorded prints, CVD renders only where prints exist, with a partial-history marker and a stated "history starts at <ts>" message consistent with the recorder's surfaced state (E16).
- Descriptor registration: `volume` (unit `qty`), `volume_ma`, `obv`, `cmf` (unit `ratio`), `mfi` (unit `ratio`), all `confidence: exact`, cadence `on_bar_close` except `cvd` which also updates `on_trade`.
- `US-MKT-006` dependency honoured: CVD requires trade prints; when the symbol is not recorded the indicator states what it needs rather than rendering an empty or zeroed series.

## Out of scope
- The dedicated CVD pane with reset anchors and divergence UI (E23), footprint (E18), Deep-Stats (E20) - all consume this kernel later.
- Recorder behaviour itself (E16); this story only consumes the "history starts at <ts>" state it publishes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Volume histogram
  Then per-bar volume renders with up/down encoding by pattern and colour, and an average-volume line is optional

Scenario: Classic CVD
  Then CVD as an indicator matches the dedicated CVD pane exactly for the same reset anchor, asserted against the shared fixture that E23 also consumes

Scenario: Missing tick data
  Given a range predates recorded prints
  Then CVD renders only where prints exist, with a partial-history marker

Scenario: Symbol is not recorded at all
  Given the symbol has no recorded prints
  Then the CVD indicator states what it requires and renders nothing, rather than drawing a flat zero line

Scenario: One delta computation serves all consumers
  Given CVD, the footprint aggregation and Deep-Stats all need bar delta for the same symbol and bar spec
  Then the kernel computes delta once per bar and serves it to all three, asserted by a call-count test

Scenario: MFI handles a zero-volume synthetic bar
  Given a densified synthetic bar with volume 0
  Then MFI carries the previous value forward under the stated rule and never divides by zero
```

## Technical notes / design
Each indicator is a plugin against the E13-T01 `IndicatorPlugin` interface (<=150 lines per `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12) and a matching `MetricDescriptor` registration in the E13-T02 backend kernel (M9). The two implementations are held together by shared golden-vector fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/` and the parity assertion established by E13-K01. Every indicator declares `warmup_bars`; values before warmup are absent, never zero. No indicator reads wall-clock time. Styling comes from `color.indicator.palette[]` and the dash ladder defined by E13-D04 - never a hard-coded colour. Delta is `buy_volume - sell_volume` from `TradeEvent` aggression side (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2) - it is never inferred from candle direction, and a test asserts that. CVD is the running sum from the anchor; `since_load` anchoring must be stable across a reload (it re-anchors and says so, rather than silently producing a different series). Volume up/down encoding uses a hatch/solid pattern pair from the E13-D04 ladder so greyscale still reads.

## Test plan
Unit: golden vectors for OBV/CMF/MFI; delta-from-aggression-side assertion; CVD anchor variants; zero-volume synthetic bar handling. Integration: partial-history rendering against a fixture whose recording starts mid-day; the shared-delta call-count test. Parity: worker mirror vs kernel. E2E: add volume histogram + volume MA, confirm greyscale distinguishability via a visual test. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model. CVD over a long unrecorded range could provoke an expensive backfill query; the range requested is bounded to the loaded window plus a prefetch margin, and the "history starts at <ts>" path short-circuits before querying storage for data known not to exist.

## Accessibility notes
Series must be distinguishable without colour: each gets a distinct dash pattern from the E13-D04 ladder. State (warming up, provisional, errored) is stated in text in the legend, never by colour alone. Legend values and per-instance names are published into the E11 DOM-mirror layer with the announcement cadence set by E13-D05. Every control introduced is reachable and operable from SCR-036. Volume up/down must be distinguishable by pattern in greyscale (US-IND-006 scenario explicitly requires pattern *and* colour); the partial-history marker is text-labelled and announced.

## Performance notes
Budgets: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars (SCR-034); parameter re-tune of the visible window <=100 ms (SCR-035); ten active indicators must not drop the scene below 55 fps (US-IND-001 NFR) and never below the 30 fps floor (budget #2). The volume histogram is a per-visible-bar instanced quad pass; it must not add a draw call per bar.

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}` (ERROR log with both values and bar index on any mismatch), `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`; analytics `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`. - [ ] Coverage: >=85% on `packages/chart-engine` / `services/api/orderflow`, >=80% on `apps/web` for new/changed lines.

Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.

title: Session and anchored VWAP as indicators with sigma envelopes
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-007** (Must/Should): "I want session VWAP with envelopes as an indicator (not only a drawing), so that it is part of my template." Its NFR is explicit: "uses the same incremental VWAP kernel as US-DRAW-005" - the anchored-VWAP drawing tool in E14. Two VWAP implementations would produce two answers for the same anchor, which is exactly the failure the epic's shared-kernel rule exists to prevent. `vwap(session)` and `vwap(session, ±1σ, ±2σ)` are already built-in presets in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §10.5.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `vwap` kernel + plugin with an `anchor` parameter: `session` (UTC day boundary by default), `utc_day`, `week`, `month`, `funding` (resets at each funding settlement for the symbol), `custom_ts`.
- Sigma envelopes: toggleable 1σ/2σ/3σ bands with labelled values, rendered as bands with the E13-D04 alpha.
- Reset marking: the reset point is marked on the chart with a glyph and a text label so a reset is never inferred from a discontinuity alone.
- Kernel shared with the E14 anchored-VWAP drawing: one incremental implementation with `snapshot()`/`restore()`, consumed by both the indicator instance and the drawing; a cross-consumer test asserts identical values for the same anchor timestamp.
- Descriptor: `vwap`, unit `price`, inputs `trades` + `bars`, cadence `on_trade`, `confidence: exact`, `warmup_bars: 0` with `nullable_when` stating that the value is None before the first print after the anchor.
- Funding-anchored behaviour uses the symbol's actual funding settlement times from the instrument metadata, not a hard-coded 8-hour assumption.

## Out of scope
- The anchored-VWAP *drawing tool* UI (E14 / US-DRAW-005) - this story ships the kernel it shares and the indicator form.
- Volume-profile-derived VWAP variants (E19).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Session VWAP
  Given the day boundary is UTC 00:00
  Then VWAP resets at the boundary and the reset is marked on the chart

Scenario: Envelopes
  When I enable 1/2/3σ envelopes
  Then they render as toggleable bands with labelled values

Scenario: Anchor options
  When I set the anchor to funding time
  Then VWAP resets at each funding settlement for the symbol, using the symbol's actual settlement schedule

Scenario: One kernel, one answer
  Given an anchored-VWAP drawing and a VWAP indicator anchored at the same timestamp
  Then both report identical values at every bar, asserted by a cross-consumer test

Scenario: No prints since the anchor
  Given the anchor is in the future or no trade has occurred since it
  Then no value is emitted, the legend states why, and no line is drawn at the last price
```

## Technical notes / design
Each indicator is a plugin against the E13-T01 `IndicatorPlugin` interface (<=150 lines per `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12) and a matching `MetricDescriptor` registration in the E13-T02 backend kernel (M9). The two implementations are held together by shared golden-vector fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/` and the parity assertion established by E13-K01. Every indicator declares `warmup_bars`; values before warmup are absent, never zero. No indicator reads wall-clock time. Styling comes from `color.indicator.palette[]` and the dash ladder defined by E13-D04 - never a hard-coded colour. VWAP is `Σ(price × volume) / Σ(volume)` over prints since the anchor - typical price (`hlc3`) is offered as a source option but the default is trade price, and which is in use is stated in the legend. Sigma bands use the volume-weighted standard deviation of price about the VWAP, not a simple stdev; the fixture discriminates them. The incremental kernel keeps running sums and must be restartable mid-session from a `snapshot()`, because replay seek (E26) primes from a checkpoint rather than replaying the day.

## Test plan
Unit: golden vectors per anchor type; volume-weighted-vs-simple stdev discrimination; snapshot/restore mid-session; funding-anchor schedule read from instrument metadata including a symbol whose schedule differs. Integration: cross-consumer identity test with the E14 drawing kernel (stubbed if E14 has not landed, then re-run as a joint test once it has). E2E: enable envelopes, change anchor, confirm the reset marker. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model. `custom_ts` anchors are bounded to the loaded/recorded range so an arbitrary far-past anchor cannot trigger an unbounded historical scan.

## Accessibility notes
Series must be distinguishable without colour: each gets a distinct dash pattern from the E13-D04 ladder. State (warming up, provisional, errored) is stated in text in the legend, never by colour alone. Legend values and per-instance names are published into the E11 DOM-mirror layer with the announcement cadence set by E13-D05. Every control introduced is reachable and operable from SCR-036. The reset marker carries a text label; envelope bands are labelled with their sigma multiple and current value; band boundaries are distinguishable without colour.

## Performance notes
Budgets: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars (SCR-034); parameter re-tune of the visible window <=100 ms (SCR-035); ten active indicators must not drop the scene below 55 fps (US-IND-001 NFR) and never below the 30 fps floor (budget #2). VWAP updates `on_trade` rather than `on_bar_close`, so its update path is on the hot ingestion route - the incremental update must be O(1) per print and is benchmarked as one of the E13-K01 worst cases.

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}` (ERROR log with both values and bar index on any mismatch), `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`; analytics `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`. Plus a log on each anchor reset with the anchor type and timestamp, so a disputed reset can be reconstructed.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass via automated tests that name the scenario.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% on `packages/chart-engine` / `services/api/orderflow`, >=80% on `apps/web` for new/changed lines.

## Dependencies
E13-S02 (kernel seam); E14 US-DRAW-005 shares this kernel (E13 owns it, E14 consumes it - coordinated via the cross-consumer test). Instrument metadata for funding schedules comes from E08's instruments cache.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). title: Expose every enabled indicator as a named metric for alerts and rules
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-008** (Must): "As a rule author, I want every enabled indicator's values exposed as named metrics, so that alerts and rules can reference exactly what I see." Its NFR is the contract: "metric identity is stable across sessions (key, not display name); resolution failures surface at save time, never silently at runtime." This story closes the loop `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 opens - "This is what makes the rule vocabulary and the indicator list the same list" - and provides the referential guard that stops an armed rule from being orphaned.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Metric naming**: every indicator instance publishes a stable metric key of the form `<indicator>(<params>, <timeframe>)` - e.g. `ema(21, 5m)` - derived from the E13-T01 instance key, stable across sessions and independent of the display name the user may have set in SCR-036.
- **Vocabulary exposure**: the enabled-indicator metrics appear in the alert editor (SCR-091) and the rule editors' metric pickers with their current value shown, sourced from the registry rather than from a frontend list.
- **Ambiguity resolution**: two EMA(21) instances with different sources are each listed with a distinguishing label (source and, if needed, instance ordinal) and each gets its own metric key.
- **Referential guard**: removing an indicator referenced by an armed rule or alert is blocked; the blocking dialog lists the referencing rules/alerts and offers disarm or edit in place, per the US-IND-008 scenario. The check is server-side authoritative (a client-side-only guard would be bypassable by an API call) and the endpoint returns the referencing objects so the dialog can render them.
- **Save-time resolution**: an alert or rule referencing a metric key that cannot be resolved fails validation at save time with the unresolvable key named - never at runtime.
- Registry surface for consumers: a `resolve(name, scope) -> MetricValue` path consistent with `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.6.

## Out of scope
- The alert editor and rule editor UIs themselves (E40, E36/E37) - this story provides the vocabulary, the current values and the guard; those epics render them.
- Rule execution semantics (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Metric available
  Given EMA(21) is on my 5m chart
  Then `ema(21, 5m)` is selectable in the alert and rule editors with its current value shown

Scenario: Ambiguity resolved
  Given two EMA(21) instances with different sources exist
  Then each is listed with a distinguishing label and its own metric key

Scenario: Removed indicator in use
  When I remove an indicator referenced by an armed rule
  Then removal is blocked with the list of referencing rules, and I can disarm or edit them from there

Scenario: Identity survives a session
  Given a rule references ema(21, 5m) and the app is restarted
  Then the same indicator instance resolves to the same key and the rule remains valid, even if the user renamed the instance in SCR-036

Scenario: Unresolvable reference fails at save time
  When a rule is saved referencing a metric key that no longer exists
  Then the save is rejected naming the unresolvable key, and the rule is never armed in an unresolvable state

Scenario: The guard cannot be bypassed from the client
  When a DELETE is issued directly against an indicator instance referenced by an armed rule
  Then the server rejects it with the referencing objects listed, independently of any client-side check
```

## Technical notes / design
The metric key is canonical: parameters are serialised in a fixed order with normalised numeric formatting, so `ema(21,5m)` and `ema(21.0, 5m)` are the same key. Display names are metadata and never participate in identity. The referential guard queries rule and alert definitions for key references; because rules compile to an IR (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md`), the reference extraction reads the IR rather than parsing editor state - that is the only representation guaranteed to be complete for both the form and node editors. Provisional values (E13-S05) are never publishable as metrics.

## Test plan
Unit: key canonicalisation including numeric normalisation and parameter ordering; ambiguity labelling with 2+ instances; reference extraction from a compiled IR covering both editor origins. Integration: removal blocked with referencing objects returned; disarm-then-remove succeeds; save-time validation rejects an unresolvable key. E2E: add EMA, create an alert on it, attempt removal, see the block, disarm from the dialog, remove successfully. Security test: direct API delete attempt bypassing the UI. Coverage >=85% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model. The specific threat here is **tampering / integrity of an armed automation**: if a referenced metric can silently disappear, an armed rule could evaluate against a missing value. Controls: server-side authoritative guard, save-time resolution, and the rule that an unresolvable reference blocks arming. Authorization: the referencing-objects list must be filtered to what the caller may see, so the guard does not leak another user's rule names - assert this with a cross-user test. Flagged for the E13-X01 threat model.

## Accessibility notes
The blocking dialog is a proper alert dialog with focus trapped, the referencing rules as a navigable list, and each disarm/edit action separately named. Current-value display in a picker is announced with the metric name and unit, not as a bare number.

## Performance notes
Metric resolution for a picker must be a single registry read per key, memoised per cadence - opening the alert editor with twenty enabled indicators must not trigger twenty recomputations. Referential-guard queries are indexed; the removal path stays interactive (<200 ms).

## Observability
`metric_resolution_failures_total{key}` (should be zero in steady state), `indicator_removal_blocked_total`, audit entries when a rule is disarmed from the blocking dialog. Log unresolvable keys with the rule id at save time.

- [ ] Coverage: >=85% on `packages/chart-engine` / `services/api/orderflow`, >=80% on `apps/web` for new/changed lines.

## Dependencies
E13-S04 and E13-S06 (so the exposed vocabulary covers the metric families rules actually need - ATR, MAs, CVD/delta), E13-S01 (the removal flow this story augments). Consumed by E35/E36/E37 (rules) and E40 (alerts); references `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md` for the IR the guard reads.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.

title: Indicator plugin API and worker-hosted runtime in packages/chart-engine
body:
## Context
The engine design already fixes the contract (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12): "Indicator plugin - pure computation over a `BarStore` producing one or more output series; runs in the worker; declares inputs, parameters, outputs, pane placement and default styling. Computation is incremental (`update(lastBar)`) with a `recompute(range)` fallback", and each built-in must be "<= 150 lines against the plugin API". This task builds that runtime so that every v1 indicator story (S02..S07) is a small plugin, and so that R2's order-flow series register through the same seam instead of forking the render path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/src/plugins/indicator/` implementing the published interface verbatim:
  `IndicatorPlugin { readonly id; readonly params: ParamSpec[]; readonly outputs: OutputSpec[]; compute(bars, params, out); update(bars, params, out, from); }`
- `IndicatorHost` running in the engine worker: registration, instance lifecycle (`addIndicator(plugin, params) -> IndicatorHandle` per the published `ChartApi`), parameter change, disposal, and deterministic instance ids stable across sessions (key, not display name - US-IND-008 NFR).
- `OutputBuffers`: typed-array output allocation and growth, `NaN`/`null` semantics for the warmup region (values before `warmup_bars` are absent, never 0), and the `provisional` flag channel for unconfirmed values.
- Incremental scheduling: `update()` on bar close; `recompute(range)` on parameter change, source change, symbol/timeframe switch, historical backfill prepend, and the late-trade `amended=True` bar re-emit path from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §5.
- Gap handling: consume `BarSeries.densify()` for indicators that need a continuous index; disable time-based indicators over renko series with the explanatory tooltip the internal-schemas doc requires.
- Render binding: outputs drawn through CMP-194 IndicatorOverlay (line/stepped/area/band/histogram) and CMP-195 AnnotationMarker (flips, pivots), with pane placement `price` | `sub` | `both` honoured and CMP-199 ChartLegend values fed per crosshair position.
- Back-pressure/degradation: participate in the §4.2 degradation ladder - "coalesce big-trade-bubble/CVD/indicator pane redraws to every 2nd frame" - as a first-class, tested behaviour.
- A conformance test kit any plugin author runs (`assertPluginConforms`) covering incremental-vs-full equivalence, warmup, gap handling and disposal-leak checks.

## Out of scope
- The indicators themselves (S02..S07) and the backend kernel (T02).
- Presets persistence (T03) and the settings UI (S01).
- WebGPU backend; user-authored scripting (explicit non-goals in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Incremental equals full
  Given any registered plugin and a 100k-bar series
  When the series is computed fully and then recomputed by appending bars one at a time through update()
  Then every output value is identical, verified by a property-based test over randomly generated bar series

Scenario: Warmup is absent, not zero
  Given an indicator with warmup_bars = 34 and 20 loaded bars
  Then no output value is emitted, the legend states how many more bars are needed, and no zero-valued series is drawn

Scenario: A parameter change recomputes the visible window first
  Given EMA(21) on a 100k-bar chart
  When the period changes to 34
  Then the visible window is recomputed and painted within 100 ms and the off-screen ranges backfill afterwards in the worker without blocking a frame

Scenario: Degradation sheds frequency, not correctness
  Given the engine is under the §4.2 worst-case load
  Then indicator pane redraws coalesce to every second frame and the computed values remain complete and correct

Scenario: A misbehaving plugin cannot take down the chart
  Given a plugin that throws inside compute()
  Then the instance enters an errored state, the error is stated in text in the legend, other indicators keep rendering, and the chart does not crash
```

## Technical notes / design
The host owns all buffers; plugins write into provided `OutputBuffers` and never allocate per-update - this is what keeps the per-frame allocation cost off the GC path. Recompute is range-scoped and chunked across frames with a stated settling allowance (<=3 frames for a hard jump, matching `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.1's `Home`/`End` allowance). Instance identity: `key = sha1(indicatorId + canonical(params) + sourceSeriesId)` truncated - stable across sessions and the same key the metric exposure in S08 uses. No plugin may read wall-clock time; determinism is asserted by replaying the same bars twice and comparing.

## Test plan
Unit: buffer growth, warmup boundaries, disposal, errored-instance isolation, renko/time-indicator guard. Property-based: incremental-vs-full equivalence over generated series including gaps, single-bar days and late amendments. Perf: micro-benchmark of `update()` at 1/10/100 instances; the 10-indicator scene benchmark lives in E13-Q03. Coverage target >=85% on the package.

## Security notes
Plugins are first-party TypeScript compiled into the bundle - there is no dynamic code loading and none must be introduced (scripting is explicitly out of scope). Parameter values arriving from persisted presets are validated against `ParamSpec` bounds before reaching a plugin, so a tampered preset cannot drive an unbounded loop (see E13-X01 CPU-exhaustion threat).

## Accessibility notes
The host publishes per-instance name, parameters, current value and state (warming up / provisional / errored) into the E11 DOM-mirror a11y layer so the legend is readable by a screen reader; announcement cadence is throttled per E13-D05.

## Performance notes
Budget: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars; parameter re-tune visible window <=100 ms. Memory: indicators share the <=8 MB "profile / indicators / drawings" allocation in the engine memory table - the host enforces a ceiling and sheds the oldest off-screen recompute buffers first.

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase=full|incremental}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_instance_errors_total{indicator}`, `indicator_active_instances{indicator}` exported through the engine's existing stats channel.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified with attached test output or measurement.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met on the touched package (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend).
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated where a design decision was made.
- [ ] SAST/SCA clean or triaged.
- [ ] perf benchmark recorded where labelled `perf`.
- [ ] QA verification recorded where the change is user-observable.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with required approvals/checks.

## Dependencies
E13-K01 fixes which indicators the worker owns. E11 supplies the scene graph, pane stacking, worker plumbing and DOM-mirror layer; E12 supplies `BarStore`/`BarSeries.densify()` and the amended-bar path.

## Branch
`feat/e13-indicators-plugin-runtime`; split into 2-3 PRs (interface + host, buffers + scheduling, render binding) to stay <=400 LOC each.

title: Backend indicator kernel (M9), MetricRegistry bindings and GET /indicators
body:
## Context
US-IND-002's NFR is the whole point of this task: "shared indicator kernel used by chart, alerts, rule engine and backtest - one implementation, one result." `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 says the `MetricRegistry` "is a single named registry ... This is what makes the rule vocabulary and the indicator list the same list", and `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` O4 makes the backend authoritative for any indicator a rule can reference. This task builds the authoritative kernel in module **M9** (`services/api/orderflow/`, CONSTITUTION.md §3) and the catalogue endpoint the UI renders its forms from.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/orderflow/indicators/` kernel: pure functions over a bar window, incremental state objects with `snapshot()`/`restore()` so a restart or a replay seek resumes without recomputing a day, memoised per `(symbol, spec_hash, params)` so "ten rules referencing `atr(14)` cost one computation" (`24-internal-schemas.md` §7).
- `MetricDescriptor` registration for every v1 indicator with the fields the schema mandates: `name`, `title`, `unit`, `value_type`, `scope`, `inputs`, `params`, `warmup_bars`, `cadence`, `nullable_when`, `deterministic`, `confidence`. All v1 TA indicators are `confidence="exact"` except heuristic-flavoured outputs (divergence flags) which are `"estimated"`.
- Extend the §7.2 catalogue entries that already exist (`atr`, `ema`, `sma`, `rsi`, `adx`, `swing_high`/`swing_low`, `realized_vol`, `parkinson_vol`, `garman_klass_vol`, `cvd`, `delta`) rather than duplicating them, and add the missing v1 names (`wma`, `vwma`, `smma`, `dema`, `tema`, `vwap`, `bollinger`, `keltner`, `donchian`, `macd`, `stochastic`, `cci`, `williams_r`, `supertrend`, `zigzag`, `ichimoku`, `psar`, `volume`, `volume_ma`, `obv`, `cmf`, `mfi`).
- `GET /api/v1/indicators` implementing `listIndicators` exactly as specified: returns `IndicatorDescriptor` items with `id`, `name`, `category` (trend|momentum|volatility|volume|orderflow), `pane` (price|sub|both), `compute` (client_worker|server per the E13-K01 assignment table), `estimated`, `params_schema` (JSON Schema the settings form renders from), `defaults`. RBAC `marketdata:read`, scope none.
- Server-computed indicator delivery: for `compute: server` descriptors, values are published on the existing market-data WS as a derived series keyed by the same instance key the engine uses (topic and framing per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, reusing E17's snapshot+delta contract - no new transport).
- Golden-vector fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/` (input bars + expected outputs per indicator) that both the Python kernel and the TypeScript mirror consume - this is the mechanism that makes "one result" testable.

## Out of scope
- Order-flow metrics that read `orderflow_metrics` (footprint/profile/CVD pane/OI/funding) - E18/E19/E23/E24 register through this same kernel later.
- The rule engine and alert evaluation themselves (E35/E40) - this task only publishes the vocabulary.
- Preset persistence (T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Values match a reference implementation
  Given the recorded Bybit BTCUSDT fixture symbol-day
  When each v1 indicator is computed by the kernel
  Then every value matches the reference implementation to 1e-8 (US-IND-002)

Scenario: One computation serves many consumers
  Given ten registered consumers all requesting atr(14) for the same symbol and bar spec
  Then the kernel computes it once per cadence and serves the memoised value, verified by a call-count assertion

Scenario: The catalogue drives the form
  When GET /api/v1/indicators is called
  Then every v1 indicator is returned with a valid JSON Schema params_schema, and adding a new indicator to the registry changes the response with no frontend change required

Scenario: Warmup is honoured
  Given atr(14) with 10 bars of history
  Then the value is None, nullable_when states exactly why, and no zero is emitted

Scenario: A bar is amended late
  Given a late trade re-emits a closed bar with amended=True
  Then the affected indicator values are recomputed from that bar forward and republished, and downstream consumers see the corrected series
```

## Technical notes / design
Constraint C3 (`24-internal-schemas.md` §1): analytics may use `float`/`numpy` inside engines, but any value crossing into OMS, journal or audit is converted via `Decimal(str(x)).quantize(...)` at the boundary - the kernel is float-internal, the boundary is explicit and tested. Wilder-smoothed indicators (ATR, ADX, RSI) must use Wilder smoothing, not EMA with alpha=1/n, and the fixture asserts it. VWAP uses the same incremental kernel as the anchored-VWAP drawing (US-IND-007 NFR, shared with US-DRAW-005). `spec_hash` is the canonical hash of `(indicator_id, params, bar_spec, source)` and is the same identity the engine's instance key derives from, so cache, metric name and UI instance agree.

## Test plan
Unit: golden vectors per indicator; Wilder-vs-EMA discrimination tests; warmup boundaries; `snapshot()`/`restore()` round-trip mid-series. Property-based: incremental equals full over generated series. Contract: `GET /indicators` validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` in the OpenAPI contract suite; every `params_schema` is itself validated as legal JSON Schema. Integration: kernel over the recorded Bybit fixture day including a gap and a late amendment. Coverage >=85% on M9.

## Security notes
`GET /indicators` is authenticated and RBAC-gated (`marketdata:read`) though the data is non-sensitive. The real surface is resource exhaustion: `compute: server` indicators let an authenticated user schedule backend work by adding chart instances - the kernel enforces a per-user cap on distinct `spec_hash` subscriptions and a parameter-bound check (period 1..5000 per SCR-035 validation) before admitting a computation. `params_schema` is server-authored static metadata, never echoed user input.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend). The `title`, `unit` and `nullable_when` fields exist so the UI can produce meaningful screen-reader text rather than raw ids - populate them for every indicator.

## Performance notes
Per-bar incremental update for the full v1 set on one symbol must stay within the ingestion stage budget (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §6.1, backend-internal <=20 ms p95 for the fan-out path). Memoisation is measured: a benchmark asserts that N consumers of the same spec cost O(1) computations.

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator}`, `indicator_cache_hits_total` / `..._misses_total`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason=amended|param_change|backfill}`, `indicator_subscriptions{user}`. Errors logged with symbol, spec_hash and bar index.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified with attached test output or measurement.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met on the touched package (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend).

## Dependencies
E13-K01 assignment table; E12 bar builders (M8) supply the bars; E17 supplies the WS transport used to publish `server`-computed series.

title: Indicator presets: migration, CRUD endpoints and built-in seed data
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.4 already specifies the `indicator_presets` table and §10.5 lists the built-in presets to seed (`ema(9)`, `ema(21)`, `ema(50)`, `ema(200)`, `vwap(session)`, `vwap(session, ±1σ, ±2σ)`, `atr(14)`, `cvd(session reset)`, `cvd(never reset)`, `delta(bar)`, ...). `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` already specifies `/indicator-presets` GET/POST and `/indicator-presets/{presetId}` PUT/DELETE with `IndicatorPreset`/`IndicatorPresetInput`. This task implements them so US-IND-001's "save as default for this indicator" control on SCR-035 and SCR-034's favourites/recents have a backing store.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Migration in `0011_workspace` (or a follow-on migration if `0011` has already shipped) creating `indicator_presets` exactly as specified, including `ux_ip_name` (unique per owner+code+lower(name) where not deleted) and `ix_ip_fav`, and the `ip_target` / `ip_code` check constraints.
- Seeding of the §10.5 built-in presets with `owner_user_id = NULL`, `is_builtin = true`; the seed is idempotent and re-runnable.
- `GET /api/v1/indicator-presets` (`listIndicatorPresets`), `POST` (`createIndicatorPreset`), `PUT /{presetId}` (`updateIndicatorPreset`), `DELETE /{presetId}` (`deleteIndicatorPreset`) - soft delete via `deleted_at`, never a hard delete.
- Validation: `params` validated against the indicator's `params_schema` from T02 before persistence; `style` validated against the closed token-name list from E13-D04; `pane_target` in (`overlay`,`subpane`); size caps on both JSONB columns.
- Authorization: a user may read built-ins plus their own presets and may only mutate their own; built-ins are immutable (a "customise" action copies to a user-owned row). RBAC `workspaces:read` / `workspaces:write`, scope self.
- `WorkspaceBundle.indicator_presets` export/import path honoured (the bundle schema already carries `IndicatorPresetInput[]`) - import is credential-free and re-validated, never trusted.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-034/035 UI that consumes these (E13-S01).
- Chart templates and workspace persistence of the indicator stack (E15).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Built-ins are present and immutable
  Given a fresh database
  When the seed runs and a user attempts to PUT a built-in preset
  Then all presets from docs/plan/21-database-schema.md §10.5 exist with is_builtin=true and the mutation is rejected with 403

Scenario: Cross-user access is denied
  Given user A owns a preset
  When user B requests, updates or deletes it
  Then the response is 404 (not 403, so existence is not disclosed) and an authorization-denied event is recorded

Scenario: Invalid params are rejected at the boundary
  When a preset is created with a period of 0 or 10000 for an indicator whose params_schema bounds it to 1..5000
  Then the API returns 422 with the offending field named and nothing is persisted

Scenario: Names are unique per user and indicator
  Given user A already has an ema preset named "Fast"
  When they create another ema preset named "fast"
  Then the request is rejected by the ux_ip_name constraint with a clear message, and the existing preset is untouched

Scenario: Deletion is reversible at the data layer
  When a preset is deleted
  Then deleted_at is set, the row remains, and it no longer appears in list responses
```

## Technical notes / design
Style validation is the reason the token list must be closed: persisting arbitrary strings into `style` and later feeding them to the renderer would be an injection seam. JSONB size caps (params <=4 KB, style <=4 KB) prevent a storage-abuse vector. The `coalesce(owner_user_id, '000...'::uuid)` in the unique index means built-ins share a namespace - the seed must not collide with it.

## Test plan
Unit: validation, authorization matrix (owner/manager/viewer x own/other/built-in), soft-delete semantics. Migration test: up/down against a seeded database, plus the idempotent re-seed. Contract: all four operations validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Integration: create -> list -> update -> delete -> export bundle -> import bundle round-trip. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: broken object-level authorization (mitigated by the 404-on-foreign-object rule and a test matrix), stored-payload abuse via JSONB (size caps + schema validation), and import of a hostile `WorkspaceBundle` (re-validated on import, `is_builtin` and `owner_user_id` never honoured from the payload). Data classification: user preference data, not secrets - but the RBAC scope is still `self` and is asserted by test.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (API). Error messages must be human-readable strings suitable for direct display in SCR-035's inline validation.

## Performance notes
Preset lists are small (tens of rows); a single indexed query per user. No budget risk; the only perf note is that the seed runs at migration time, not on every boot.

## Observability
Audit/analytics events on create/update/delete with `{indicator_code, preset_id}`; metric `indicator_presets_total{builtin}`; authorization denials logged with actor, target and reason.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified with attached test output or measurement.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met on the touched package (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend).
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated where a design decision was made.

title: ADR for indicator compute placement and parity, plus plan-doc updates
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` states that "Resolution of O4 must be recorded as an amendment to ADR-0007 (rule IR) if it changes which indicators are rule-eligible". E13-K01 produces the decision; this task lands it as a durable record and reconciles the plan docs with what was actually built, as the Epic DoD requires ("docs reflect final shipped behavior, not the original proposal").

## Scope / Deliverables
- New ADR `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0019-indicator-compute-placement.md`: context (O4 and the rule-engine constraint), decision (per-indicator `compute` assignment table), consequences (worker mirror is display-only; the parity contract and its epsilon; what changes if an indicator later becomes rule-eligible), alternatives rejected, and the benchmark evidence from E13-K01.
- Amendment to `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md` if and only if rule eligibility changed, stating which metric names became rule-referenceable and what that obliges of the compiler.
- Close open question **O4** in `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §14/open-questions table, replacing it with a pointer to the ADR, and correct the "bit-for-bit" wording there if K01 established an epsilon instead.
- Update `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2 with the v1 indicator metric rows actually registered (names, params, defaults, warmup, cadence, confidence).
- Update `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-034/035/036 entries where implementation diverged from the catalogue, and fix the known inconsistency in SCR-034 where the A11y line cites US-CHART-008 while the Stories line cites US-IND-001..007.
- Changelog fragment for R1 describing the indicator capability in user-facing terms.

## Out of scope
- Re-litigating the decision; this is a recording task.
- Writing end-user documentation (R5 docs epic E48).

## Acceptance criteria

title: STRIDE threat model and abuse cases for the indicator framework
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 require a STRIDE threat model per Epic. E13 looks low-risk (market data and presentation preferences) but has four real surfaces: a server-supplied JSON Schema rendered into a form, user-controlled JSONB persisted as preset params and styles, authenticated users scheduling backend computation via `compute: server` indicators, and an integrity path where ATR feeds `sl_offset_unit="atr"` stop sizing and Zig Zag swings could feed structure-based trailing stops. The last of those makes an "indicators are just cosmetics" assumption dangerous.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE model document `docs/security/threat-models/e13-indicators.md` covering the data flows: browser <-> `GET /indicators`, browser <-> `/indicator-presets`, kernel -> MetricRegistry -> rule/alert consumers, worker mirror -> display, and `WorkspaceBundle` import.
- Per-element STRIDE enumeration with at least these threats analysed and dispositioned:
  - **Spoofing/Elevation**: reading or mutating another user's presets (broken object-level authorization); built-in presets mutated by a non-owner.
  - **Tampering**: a hand-edited preset or imported bundle carrying out-of-range params, an unknown `indicator_code`, a style value that is not an enumerated token, or `is_builtin: true`; a provisional Zig Zag swing reaching a rule; a worker-computed (display-only) value being used where the authoritative kernel value is required - specifically for ATR-based stop offsets.
  - **Repudiation**: preset and indicator changes without audit/analytics events.
  - **Information disclosure**: the E13-S08 referencing-objects list leaking another user's rule or alert names; error messages echoing internal paths.
  - **Denial of service**: parameter-driven CPU exhaustion (period 5000 x many instances) in the worker and in the backend kernel; unbounded `compute: server` subscriptions per user; unbounded sub-pane creation; oversized JSONB in `params`/`style`; an unbounded historical backfill triggered by a far-past `custom_ts` VWAP anchor.
- **Abuse cases** written as executable statements handed to E13-Q06 (black-box) and E13-X02 (verified): each with a concrete request/action, the expected rejection, and the observable evidence.
- Control recommendations mapped to owning tickets (T02 caps and param bounds, T03 authorization and validation, S05 provisional exclusion, S08 server-side guard and filtered listing) - each either already in scope or filed as a new ticket.
- Data classification statement: market data (public), presentation preferences (user-private), and the note that indicator values become *safety-relevant* the moment a rule or a stop offset consumes them.

## Out of scope
- The rule engine's own threat model (E35) and the OMS/fan-out model (E29/E34) - this model hands off the metric-integrity boundary to them explicitly.
- Penetration testing (E43, pre-R4).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every data flow is analysed
  Then each of the five enumerated data flows has a STRIDE row per category with either a threat and a control or an explicit "not applicable" with a reason

Scenario: The safety-relevant path is called out
  Then the model states explicitly that ATR feeds sl_offset_unit="atr" per-account profiles and that a display-only worker value must never be the source for a stop offset, with the control and its owning test named

Scenario: Abuse cases are executable
  Given the abuse-case list is handed to QA
  Then each case states the exact action, the expected rejection and how to observe it, with no interpretation required

Scenario: Every control has an owner
  Then each recommended control maps to an existing E13 ticket or a newly filed ticket, and no control is left as an unassigned recommendation
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the STRIDE-per-element method over a DFD drawn in mermaid inside the model document. Reuse the control vocabulary from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` so findings map onto the existing SR-nnn requirement ids where they apply. The DoS analysis should use the measured numbers from E13-K01/Q03 rather than guessing at cost.

## Test plan
The model's abuse cases are the test plan; verification is E13-X02 plus the QA charter in E13-Q06. The model itself is reviewed by the Architect and the chart-engine lead as well as the Security engineer.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security artefact for E13 and supplies the Epic DoD's "STRIDE model finalized, findings triaged" evidence.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
DoS controls (parameter bounds, instance caps, JSONB size caps) must be set from the measured costs in E13-K01/E13-Q03 so limits are defensible and do not needlessly constrain legitimate use.

## Observability
Recommend the security-relevant telemetry: authorization-denial logs on preset access, `indicator_subscriptions{user}` for cap enforcement, and an ERROR-level `indicator_parity_mismatch_total` because a parity divergence on a safety-relevant metric is a security-adjacent event, not merely a bug.

- [ ] Findings recorded with STRIDE category, likelihood/impact and disposition (fix / accept with Owner sign-off).
- [ ] Mitigation tickets filed and linked; accepted risks added to `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.
- [ ] Any rules/checks produced are merged and running in CI.

title: Security review of indicator endpoints, presets and metric exposure
body:
## Context
E13-X01 enumerates the threats; this ticket verifies the controls in the built code before E13 can close. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes security sign-off non-optional for anything touching authorization boundaries, and E13 has two: preset ownership (`/indicator-presets`) and the metric-exposure guard that can list another user's referencing rules if filtered incorrectly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Code review** by the Security engineer of: `/indicator-presets` handlers and their authorization checks, the `params_schema`-driven form renderer, the bundle-import validation path, the E13-S08 referencing-objects endpoint, and the kernel's parameter-bound and subscription-cap enforcement.
- **Abuse-case execution** of every case from E13-X01, with evidence recorded per case:
  - request/modify/delete another user's preset (expect 404, not 403);
  - mutate a built-in preset (expect 403);
  - POST a preset with `is_builtin: true`, a foreign `owner_user_id`, an unknown `indicator_code`, a non-token style value, an out-of-range period, and an oversized JSONB blob (expect 422/403, nothing persisted);
  - import a hand-crafted `WorkspaceBundle` with the same payloads (expect the same rejections, with `is_builtin`/`owner_user_id` never honoured from the payload);
  - delete an indicator instance referenced by an armed rule directly via the API, bypassing the UI (expect rejection with the referencing objects, filtered to the caller's visibility);
  - request the referencing-objects list as a user who cannot see the referencing rule (expect the rule not to be named);
  - subscribe to `compute: server` indicators beyond the per-user cap (expect rejection with a clear error, no unbounded backend work).
- **SAST rules**: Semgrep rules committed under the repo's rule directory for the E13-specific anti-patterns - rendering a schema-derived string as HTML/markdown, constructing a component from a payload-supplied name, and any JSONB write that is not preceded by schema validation.
- **SCA/secrets**: confirm the new fixture directory carries no secrets and that no new dependency was introduced for indicator maths without SCA clearance.
- Findings triaged with the Owner where acceptance rather than fix is proposed; sign-off comment on E13 and on the affected stories.

## Out of scope
- DAST/ZAP scanning of the whole app (the security program's scheduled activity) and penetration testing (E43).
- The rule engine's own review (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case is executed with evidence
  Then each E13-X01 abuse case has a recorded execution with request, response, and a pass/fail judgement

Scenario: Object-level authorization holds
  Given user B attempts to read, update or delete user A's preset
  Then every attempt returns 404 without disclosing existence, and an authorization-denial event is recorded

Scenario: Hostile payloads are rejected at the boundary
  Given a bundle import carrying is_builtin true, a foreign owner id, an unknown indicator code and an oversized style blob
  Then the import is rejected with the offending fields named and nothing is persisted, including no partial import

Scenario: The referencing list does not leak
  Given an indicator is referenced by a rule the caller cannot see
  Then the removal is still blocked but the response does not name that rule, and the caller is told to contact the owner

Scenario: SAST rules catch the pattern they exist for
  Given a deliberate violation (rendering a schema-derived string as HTML) is introduced
  Then the Semgrep rule fires in CI and blocks the PR
```

## Technical notes / design
Execute abuse cases against a staging build with two seeded users of differing roles (owner and manager) plus a viewer, so the RBAC matrix is genuinely exercised rather than assumed. Record raw request/response pairs (credentials redacted) as evidence per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.

## Test plan
Abuse cases are the tests; the durable ones are promoted into the automated suite (the cross-user preset case joins E13-Q02, the payload-validation cases join the backend contract suite) so the checks survive beyond this review.

## Security notes
This ticket produces the Epic DoD's "findings triaged (fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off), sign-off comment from Security engineer" evidence.

## Accessibility notes
Error messages produced by rejected payloads must still be usable UI strings - verify they are human-readable and do not leak internal paths or stack traces.

## Performance notes
Verify the subscription cap and parameter bounds actually bound cost, using the E13-Q03 I5 measurement as the reference for what an admitted request may cost.

## Observability
Confirm each rejection emits the expected telemetry (authorization-denial log with actor/target/reason, validation-rejection counter); a silent rejection is a finding.
